items.discussion:
A. Resolution to the Common Council regarding amendments to the zoning code in regard to Accessory Dwelling Units.

Upon motion made by Chair Grunblatt and seconded by Commissioner Clement, the Commission voted to
authorize Planning Director Suzanne Cahill to draft a letter to the Common Council on the Commission's behalf
expressing the position that this legislation must not impede upon the Commission's ability to maintain their
review authority of building exteriors where applicable, that the Commission strongly opposes the removal of the
owner occupancy requirement as this helps to stabilize neighborhoods and properties, that the Council be mindful
when considering reducing the off-street parking and its implications to streets.areas that already have on street
parking limitations and congestion, and that if there are substantive changes to the legislation of any magnitude,
including changing the zones to which the amendments are being proposed, that those shall return to the
Commission for review and comment.

Julie Edelson-Safford, Historic Preservation Admin.            Steven T. Noble, Mayor

The survey will be distributed amongst the Commissioners and discussed at the next meeting.

D. Chair Grunblatt recognized the passing of Past City Historian Ed Ford and his contributions over the years in making
historic preservation in Kingston an issue that belongs on the table and is recognized throughout the community as
having importance in our identity.

The Historic Landmarks Preservation Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR. The Commission also voted to find as fact that the proposed signage for 275 Fair St. in the Stockade Historic District, by the applicant, Timely Signs of Kingston; and the owner, Opera House LLC, if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-64, of the City of Kingston’s Administrative Code, is compatible with the historic character of the building and the district for the following reasons: -that the proposed will involve two single sided stud mounted letter sets, both 120"w x 10.25"h x 1/2"thick PVC, CVC routed logo primed and painted white, the sofit to be painted Benjamin Moore Van Deusen Blue HC 156; - that this work will cause a material change to the external appearance of the property; - that the said signage will not detract from the character of the historic district or the building; - that any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; - that this Commission’s approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston’s Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 1st day of July 2021, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (SEQR: HC – motion, RT – 2nd, MG, AP, KM – yes; DEFER OPINION: MG – motion, AP – 2nd, HC, KM, RT – yes)

decisions.text: Hayes Clement stated that at the last meeting the HAC voted to defer to the HLPC. The HAC agreed to defer the decision to the HLPC. D. Barnes motion, A. Robin second. All in favor. (DB, AR, HC, KM – yes) V. Polidoro stated that there is no restriction from having a sign on the second story if the business occupies that space. The marquee would draw attention to the large space. Other businesses could seek approval install their own signs on above the Pike Plan as well. H. Clement stated that he believed that the marquee sign was not ready for review at this time due to the lack of detail and that the discussion of the marquee would be a larger conversation. R. Tonner expressed concern with the portion of the marquee that extends beyond the Pike Plan. A. Robin voiced that she felt the marquee design was charming. A Puetz stated that the design presented felt a bit large in relation to the surroundings. K. McEvoy agreed with A. Puetz that the size might be too large in scale. H. Clement focused discussion on the other two signs that are seeking approval. He stated that he felt that the current proposal is a vast improvement in both size and color from the design that was reviewed at the July meeting. Other members agreed that the changes were positive. The Commission discussed color of the painted sign, asking for consideration of a more washed look or using a color that was not bright white and black but an off white and charcoal. R. Tonner asked if the façade will be changed in any way in the future. V. Polidoro stated that it is an internal discussion but that no decisions have been made. R. Tonner said that it sticks out in its current state and not in a good way. V. Polidoro said that she would take that comment back to the client.

The commission voted to declare the action a Type II under SEQR and to adopt the Preservation Notice of Action as amended as follows: Introducing the motion that the Commissioners present find as fact that the proposed signage for 323 Wall St. in the Stockade Historic District, by the applicant, Wall Street Music Hall, LLC; and the owner, 323 Wall Street Owners, LLC, if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-64, of the City of Kingston’s Administrative Code, is compatible with the historic character of the building and the district for the following reasons: -that the proposed will involve 3 separate signs: Sign 1 will be painted directly on the southern facade of the building ("Sign 1") with the venue's name and logo directly onto the existing brick exterior. Signs 2 will be located at the front of the building along Wall Street. It will be a 4'x6' aluminum, also with the venue's name and logo, mounted to the building's exterior wooden cladding ("Sign 2"). Both Sign 1 and 2 will be either in the black and white as presented, or in an off white/cream background with charcoal lettering as discussed as an option. Sign 2 will be removed after fabrication of the proposed third "marquee" sign. Said sign will return for full review by the year end. - that this work will cause a material change to the external appearance of the property; - that the said signage will not detract from the character of the historic district or the building; - that any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; - that this Commission’s approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston’s Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 5th day of August 2021, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to endorse the finding of fact of the Preservation Notice of Action as approved by the HLPC. (BH – motion, MD – 2nd, HC, DB, JM – yes)

The HLPC voted unanimously to find as fact and adopt a Preservation Notice of Action as follows: The Historic Landmarks Preservation Commission (HLPC) for the City of Kingston makes the following findings, reached in accordance with the review procedures set forth in Section 405 -64 of the City of Kingston’s A dministrative Code. The following determinations regarding the issuance of a Preservation Notice of Action for the development proposal known as “The Kingstonian”, address material submitted by the applicant, as well as submissions by consultants and inte rested members of the public. The HLPC further notes that the evidentiary record included material offered for consideration of the closure of Fair Street Extension, massing, scale, visual elements, fire and public health/safety issues, and uses at the project site. The aforementioned material has been thoroughly reviewed and considered to determine if the project is compatible with the historic character of the Stockade Historic District. The HLPC Commissioners present find as fact that the Kingstonian, located at #9-17 & 21 North Front Street and Fair Street Extension, in the Stockade Historic District, by the Applicants, Kingstonian Development LLC and JM Development Group; and Owners, Kingstonian Development LLC and City of Kingston, if done accordin g to the plans reviewed prior to and at this meeting, is compatible with the historic character of the Stockade Historic District for the following reasons: - The proposed work is to take place at parcels presently occupied by a City of Kingston on grade parking lot, an abandoned portion of public roadway, including also two structures, a warehouse building and an abandoned restaurant, along with associated site improvements; - Based on the resources HLPC customarily consults, the HLPC understands that the existing warehouse structure does not appear on the 1858 Map of Ulster County by J. H. French, is depicted as a smaller structure on the 1870 Beers Map of Rondout, Kingston, and Wilbur; and it is shown on the 1914 Codwise Maps. That documentation on the NYS Cultural Resource Inventory System (CRIS) was studied and it is recognized under 2 entries that the structure was built in either the 1870’s or the 1880’s, as a 3 story frame hotel. That the structure was bricked over frame siding, removed porch, adding one story brick section to front and creating “L” shape, circa 1946. Though not an exhaustive list of reference materials, the HLPC can reasonably estimate the construction and historical transition of the building. - The proposed work will involve the demolition of existing structures, construction of a 420 vehicle parking garage, approximately 9,000 SF retail/restaurant space, a 32 -room boutique hotel, 143 mixed residential units, including 14 affordable units, an open pedestrian plaza with public -oriented amenities, and an Americans with Disabilities (ADA) - compliant walking bridge to connect with the adjoining Kingston Plaza; - This work will cause a material change to the external appearance of the property; - The HLPC has further reviewed the comprehensive December 16, 2019 SEQRA Negative Declaration, issued by the City of Kingston Planning Board as Lead Agency, in light of the Kingstonian Project and the Preservation Notice of Action Criteria (§405-64 B). In this regard, the HLPC agrees with the Lead Agency’s Negative Declaration statements in determining that there are no significant adverse environmental impacts posed by the Kingstonian development in terms of traffic, historic district impacts, visuals, character of neighborhood or any other areas of environmental concern (see 6 NYCRR Part 617.7); - The HLPC recognizes the intended use of colors selected from the Benjamin Moore Historic Color Collection; Branchport Brown (HC-72), Stonington Gray (HC-170), Chelsea Gray (HC-168), Monterey White (HC-27) and Kingsport Gray (HC -86); as depicted on the drawing entitled Kingston-Paint Selection, sated 2-1-22, and submitted by S. Dutton, RA; - The HLPC heard and considered a concern expressed during a public hearing regarding the reflective quality of the exterior glass depicted on a rendering of the project; the HLPC confirms that clear glass with low E coating will be utilized, as described by S. Dutton, RA. - The HLPC heard and considered various architectural concerns, raised in response to a design pre sented at the January 10, 2022 public hearing, pertaining to design elements such as recessing storefront entrances along North Front Street, provision of canopies over entries, and upgrading the corner entry, and it concludes that these have been adequate ly addressed with respect to design intent for color, scale and patterning as represented in 3D architectural renderings, prepared by S. Dutton, RA, and will be followed. - Based on the established record, the HLPC does not agree with the project opponents ’ claims that the contemplated demolition will detrimentally impact the historic character of the neighborhood or that the project as a whole is “out of scale” for the neighborhood. The HLPC also finds that concerns raised regarding the number of affordab le housing units incorporated into the Kingstonian project are beyond the scope of the Preservation Notice of Action. Moreover, the HLPC has examined the project opponents’ other conclusions, submissions, and reports and determines that the weight of extensive evidence in the administrative record supports the findings set forth herein; - In further support of this conclusion, the HLPC references and hereby incorporates the following documentation which has been submitted of record in the Kingstonian matter: 1. January 12, 2022 Letter, M. Moriello, together with exhibits annexed, as provided to City of Kingston Common Council and copied to HLPC. 2. Visual simulations, depictions and submissions offered by the Applicants and Scott Dutton, RA, to date.

items.title: #106-122 Green Street Replacement of windows and shutters
items.discussion:
Kaaren Davis and Selina Guendel were present at the meeting to represent the Wiltwyck
Chapter of the DAR.  Chairman Clement opened with recognizing the prior reviews which have taken place
and noting that the applicants at the last meeting were requested to submit information in addition to what
had already been requested, like the sample window product.  H. Clement stated that the building is a very
prominent structure and recognized within the Stockade Historic District.
It was stated that the applicants were notified the day after the meeting in an informal email outlining the June
decision and the formal decision was transmitted to them via email on June 8th.
S. Cahill was asked for staff opinion and repeated the June decisions which were:

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to table the application until the July 7, 2022 meeting noting that the application is recognized to be Incomplete at this time. The following information is requested: 1) The applicant provide the name and background of the historic professional which has been engaged to undertake a conditions assessment to the Planning Office immediately, and 2) The Final Conditions Assessment Report and any supporting documents be submitted to the Planning Office by June 30th (1 week prior to next meeting), for posting and circulation.

The Commission voted unanimously to table the application and endorse the HLPC decision to request additional information be submitted. S. Cahill reviewed staff comments as follows: • We have reviewed the submission made on July 1, 2022, which included statements from 2 separate individuals – Jeff Martino (Country Homes General Contracting) and Harley Davis (H&J Farms Contracting LLC) • Recognize that this is a “key” building in the Stockade Historic District • We see nothing in the submissions that meets what was requested by the Commissions: o Both appear to be General Contractors that would do a standard window install anywhere. Lacking credentials which were expected to be represented as a Preservation Expert would possess. o No statement that would demonstrate what a Historic Preservation Expert would typically provide as background of credentials, such as education, other similar projects, experience with tax credit projects, a resume etc… o No indication that there is any familiarity with Secretary of Interior Standards o We see deficiencies in both Conditions Survey documents. For example, one would typically have stronger, more specific documentation as part of assessment and actual conditions, i.e. photographs to document, references to Secretary of Interior Standards, individual window notations (not broad strokes as classifying groupings of windows or generalized bullet statements). o Appears that one of the parties is actually the company who you had planned to do the Marvin Window replacement installation? (NOTE: The applicants present confirmed this statement.) • Staff does not feel that either Commission is able to reference and/or rely on this information to make an informed decision. • Have in the past provided names of individuals that do this type of work, recognize that you might not want to use them, but they were typical of the caliber of expert who should be involved. • We recognize in past discussions, that this may not be an all or nothing type project, you may have to completely replace one or more windows, but there are more than likely others that can be restored. • We recognize there are other means to achieve the goals of weatherization and climate control. • SHPO - We have referred the information to SHPO and they have also concurred with our assessment. • The materials are deficient as they do not meet what was requested to make your application capable of being considered complete. S. Cahill then asked the if this is all that they plan to submit to have the application deemed complete for the Commission’s review? The applicants stated that windows present are not original to the house and that part of the problem is that they have not been maintained adequately over the years. They asked why the City has not said anything before about the conditions? Staff noted the issue before the Commissions is a result of the applicants initiating the project. It is not something the City would typically go around and look for on private properties, unless there was a public safety issue involved. A. Bornhoft noted that the age of the windows does establish a certain historic era, even if they were not the ones original when the building was first constructed. She also agrees that the conditions assessments provided, while one did have more information than the other, were not what is standard and didn’t provide enough detail information for any determination of conditions. She will provide names of individuals that may be able to assist. Assist. Corp Counsel, M. Jankowski stated that the applicant’s may consider withdrawing their application. He would also note that in a future submission the primary section of the City Code to pay attention to is §405-65 B. He encouraged the applicants to seek assistance from a professional and stressed that if they before engaging anyone, to speak with staff. It was discussed that if the application was withdrawn, with the intent to re-submit, a new application fee would not be charged. The applicant took a side conference for a few minutes and then requested to withdraw their application from consideration, noting they would work with staff to resubmit a more complete application.

The Commission voted unanimously to accept the withdrawal request, understanding that the applicants will work with staff to re-submit a complete application. A new fee will not be assessed. (MD- Motion; JM – 2nd – HC, JM – Yes)

The Commission voted unanimously to accept the withdrawal request, understanding that the applicants will work with staff to re-submit a complete application. A new fee will not be assessed. (RT – Motion, NM – 2nd – AP, HC – Yes; MG – Recused)

includes installation of banners on each of the Kinsley Hotel buildings for purposes of branding and

but the shade could be adjusted.  He also stated that the fabric would have a life span of 5-10 years given
location and weather issues.  He did note though that if one does need to be replaced sooner, it would be

items.title: #58 Pearl Street Application for painting a mural on the side of an existing building
items.discussion:
Reverend Kendra VanHouten, representing the Fair Street Church, and Linsey Wolkowicz from
O+, were present at the meeting.  The Reverend explained the location for the mural on the side of the building.
She noted that although the mural would not take up the entire building side, the base coat of paint will.  She
also noted that the existing wall sign is being relocated to where they currently have a free-standing message
board.  L. Wolkowicz gave an overview, explaining the materials to be used, the specifics of the primer and
paint, and the focus on choosing locations and murals to work together and complement each other. There is
not only thought in the locations, but care is taken to utilize materials that will help preserve/protect the

underlying building materials.  Rev. VanHouten shared a mural design with the Commissions.  The mural
presented was not the one originally shared, but the artist is the same and the style is similar in content
representation.  The new mural design was shared with the Commissions and will be sent to the Planning
Office for the file.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to adopt a Preservation Notice of Action, finding as fact that the proposed mural painting on the east facade of the building at 58 Pearl Street, in the Fair Street Historic District, by O+ Art Festival 2022 Artist Shawnee Miller and owner Fair Street Reformed Church, if done according to the plans and presentation of materials reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-64, of the City of Kingston’s Administrative Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: - The building is a brick masonry, 2 1/2 story building that presently houses the Fair Street Reformed Church Thrift Shop, is shown on the 1870 Beers and 1914 Codwise Maps, and considered to be non-contributing to the Local Fair Street Historic District ; - The project is to install a painted mural on the east facade of the structure, by artist Shawnee Miller, for a minimum of 3 years time. The work will include gentle power washing and priming the surface with a water- based acrylic to preserve the facade and prevent pigment staining. The image will be done using lightfast acrylic mural paint (architectural grade), not oil based, so no damage or penetration to existing brick underneath will occur, along with the relocation of the wall signage to the existing location where a message board currently exists; - That since the said building is a non-contributing resource to the historic district and not a principal feature of the historic district, the alteration will not detract from the character of the historic district or the building; - Any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; - The Commission’s approval does not obviate the need for any other required approvals or permits from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 27th day of September 2022, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Artist and property owner, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (SEQR – HC – motion, KM – 2nd, MG, NM – yes; Approve – MG – motion, HC – 2nd, NM, KM – yes)

HAC Adoption of the Minutes of December 1, 2022 Meeting. HLPC Adoption of the Minutes of December 1, 2022 Meeting
items.discussion:
C. Plays, applicant representative was present at the meeting alongside the project architect
Paul Jankovitz. P. Jankovitz handed out some plan sheets to Commission members to have in front of them as
they discuss the proposal.  He noted the changes made to the plans since they were last in front of the
Commissions. The owner still wishes to renovate the building, but the use is now event space and 2 retail
spaces on the Wall Street side. Improvements will include new signage, landscaping, storm drainage, lighting
in the parking area, a parking layout, and ADA accessibility.

P Jankovitz reviewed the space breakdown, noting that the larger event space will be accessed from the front
along Wall Street and the rear parking area.  Four bathrooms (1-ADA and 3 standard, all unisex) along with a
janitor closet are being constructed within the building, on the main level.  Two new retail spaces are being
created with entry from Wall Street. One space is 1291sf the other is 1262sf.  Both spaces are being provided a
separate ADA accessible/unisex bathroom.   S. Cahill noted that the owner has not secured tenants and the
applicants were advised that once they do, they will need to submit signage plans.  Signage for both will need
review of the HLPC/HAC and be consistent with the guidelines established for underneath the Pike Plan.  Staff
also noted that window signage along Wall Street should be limited to the 20% rule (Board Policy #11).  P.
Jankovitz asked if the current signage in the windows can stay, and staff noted it was not approved and will
most likely be addressed at the Planning Board level.  Overall, the Commissions were pleased to see the
addition of retail to the street face.

When questioned, C. Plays, confirmed that although there is access to the basement area from Wall Street and
access to the basement from within the event space, this area will be for storage only at this time.  If that use
changes, they will submit new plans to the staff to review and determine if additional Commission review is
needed.

P. Jankovitz reviewed the rear area (Crown Street frontage) noting that they have made certain changes to the
parking area, including added landscaping areas within the layout, but most significantly are adding 5 drywells
to the site to address the stormwater issue and ponding.  S. Cahill noted that an archeologist will be a
requirement as the project site is located in an area deemed to be archeologically sensitive.  K. McEvoy agreed
that with any excavation on site to install the dry well stormwater system or other elements, the applicants
should be required to have an archeologist on site at all times during excavation to monitor the materials being
uncovered.  He asked who it would be?  C. Plays indicated that they are using HCS (Hudson Cultural Services)
for this work.  He will provide the name and contact information as requested.  M. Grunblatt noted that the
name of the professional, credentials, and full plan for this monitoring should be submitted for review.  The
plan should have recognition of how materials will be surveyed and recorded and if the situation occurs where
an artifact of significant importance is uncovered, how that would be addressed.

S. Cahill asked Commission members to look at the proposed lighting fixtures and make any comment.  P.
Jankovitz noted that the lighting is a simple wall mount style that can be adjusted easily.  No pole lighting or
other freestanding fixtures will be installed as they are also considering the lighting from the street for
coverage.  That is the single pole, more decorative lantern style.  Commission members made no comments on
the fixture type.

The name of the business has been changed to “Kingston Studios” and the Wall Street façade will have the
similar lettering as previously approved signage under the name “Uptown Studios”.  The sign will be 3’ x 60’
with each letter fixed directly to the façade. Previous signage included lighting behind the lettering to create a
hallow effect. The Commissions confirmed that the lettering will be red, to match as closely as possible the
previous “Woolworth” lettering.   The only change being a font size alteration to fit more letters for the
buildings new title. The application materials were the height and width of the lettering at about 8’ tall and 4’
from the face of the façade. HLPC members asked for those dimensions to be submitted in writing on the
applications follow-up.  R. Tonner asked if there would be a space between the wording, as the illustration
does not indicate one?  C. Plays noted there would be, the drawing will be updated to reflect the actual.  He
also stated that the Wall Street face of the building will remain the teal color it is now but with a fresh coat of
paint.

The Commissions looked at Crown Street, and P. Jankovitz noted that the previous plans have been revised to
include a new sign stating “No. 311”.  The sign will be 4’1” x 21’10”.  The plans note that the lettering will be post
mounted to the brick with masonry anchors, LED backlighting, a sheet metal base with chrome finish cast
resign lettering.    Also being proposed are 3 overhead garage doors with aluminum frames and glass panel
windows.  The original plan included pivoting doors with signage adhered. N. Morano asked how the doors
would open and P. Jankovitz indicated they open in and would be open while events are occurring, The
existing awnings in this area will be removed and replaced with an awning with “Kingston Studios” printed

over the main entry area.  R. Tonner asked if the color shown was accurate and for a detail of the final awning
to be provided to the Commission.  P. Jankovitz stated he would prepare the document.

S. Cahill noted that they continue to show 2 dedicated spaces for food truck vending option, however, no
outdoor seating area will be provided as the service will be for the events and not for regular foot traffic off the
street.

items.title: #323 Wall Street. Install marquee sign to Wall Street face of structure (second floor level)., along with a “box” sign with changeable letters for program information
items.discussion:
P. Jankovitz, project architect and C. Plays, representing owner were present to discuss the
application.  P. Jankovitz handed out some plan sheets to Commission members to have in front of them as they
discuss the proposal.  He reviewed the proposal to install a marquee sign on the Wall Street face of building.
Although they provided two styles of signs in the submitted materials, they prefer the one which is larger and
taller, but more like the original marquee sign in style and size.  It would project outward 90 degrees from the
building face and would extend well above the existing height of the current roof line.  The sign would be
constructed of metal and steel illuminated in a similar manner as original sign. No colors were provided, but P.
Jankovitz noted that they would look at using coloring similar to the smaller scale sign shown in the materials.

M. Grunblatt asked about the full height of the proposed sign from grade?  C. Plays, stated that it would be
around 46’.

The marquee sign will have messaging provided by hand through translucent plastic pieces. R. Tonner noted
that in the materials the original marquee had a configuration that was visible from different angles and the
proposed is flat.  He also asked if there were any specific regulations about overhanging the Pike Plan structure,
noting that the sign itself is not supported in any way on the Pike Plan canopy.  S. Cahill will have to research
and determine if there are any.   P. Jankovitz noted that access for changing would prohibit an angled shape and
would require temporary closing a section of the street to allow for manually changing message.

S. Cahill would recommend that this be referred to both the City Engineer and the Building Inspector to
determine the feasibility.  C. Plays and P. Jankovitz both noted that the owner has had an engineer look at the
proposal and the design of the sign itself is going to be supported internally within the building, for a “cleaner”
look and the passed-on sheet plan documents of the structural install.  M. Grunblatt noted that the engineering
work should be referred to the City Engineer and the BSD for a review.

B. Howland asked how the new sign would be lit.  C. Plays stated that they will submit the illumination.

R. Tonner asked what might be done to the building façade given the effort to replicate the historic signage.  P.
Jankovitz and C. Plays, both spoke about the plan for the façade.  They will be removing a portion to determine
the condition of the underlying masonry, but the owner is committed to a historic brick façade restoration.  P.
Jankovitz believes that the existing siding was installed with firring strips, and they believe that little damage
is done.  They will repoint as needed and clean the brick as well.

S. Cahill suggested a visual simulation of the new sign and façade be prepared which incorporates the existing
streetscape.  Perhaps a view from the corner of Wall and John looking down to really understand how the new
sign and façade will be a feature in the streetscape.  The Commission agreed and the representatives present
stated that would be done.  Staff noted that color, size, and final design details would be important to use in
this simulation.  Lighting might also be a consideration in a version.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to table the application pending submission of materials as discussed and outlined by the HLPC. (BH – motion, NM – 2nd; KM, JM – yes)

The Commission voted unanimously to table the application pending information as follows: 1. City to research any Pike Plan restrictions that would prohibit structures above the canopy. 2. Refer the engineering design plans that were submitted to City Engineer and the BSD for review and comment/approval. 3. Method of illumination and specifications. 4. Final full façade restoration plan for Wall Street façade. 5. Final design and specifications for building signage, with color. 6. Daytime and Nighttime streetscape view simulation (from Wall and John) incorporating final signage and façade restoration into the existing streetscape, with night version. (MG – motion, NM – 2nd; RT, KM – yes)

items.title: #2-8 and 10 Crown Street. Installation of vehicular traffic directional signage
items.discussion:
P. Beichert,  Timely Signs was present to represent the owner.   The HLPC and applicant
discussed the purpose, locations and design of the signs proposed. P. Beichert noted that they wanted to keep
the signage complimentary to the historic character, and that they were trying to provide not only wayfinding,
but identification for all uses on 2 separate parcels, but under the same ownership.

R. Tonner asked if the traffic signs are enforceable.  P. Beichert stated while the traffic directional signs are
recognizable as such, they are distinguishable from actual government signs and not enforceable by law

enforcement.  M. Grunblatt confirmed the statement.  R. Tonner asked if the owner has a need to regulate users
in the parking area during weekend events?  P. Beichert was not aware of any need for additional signs, but will
refer the issue to the owner.

S. Cahill noted that the signs are not illuminated so questioned if the lettering and symbols are reflective.  P.
Beichert confirmed they have a reflective quality.

S. Cahill also noted that within the submission there is an option for an exit sign, whether to post it on a free-
standing post or on the wall face.  The Commissions strongly opposed a mounted sign on the historic building.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to recommend approval of the proposal as discussed and endorse the decision of the HLPC in adopting the PNoA. (KM- motion, NM -2nd; BH, JM – yes)

The Commission voted unanimously to recognize the proposal as a Type II Action under SEQR and approve Findings of Fact and adopt a Preservation Notice of Action as follows: The Commissioners present find as fact that the proposed renovations and restoration at 2-8 and 10 Crown Street, in the Stockade Historic District, by applicant Hudson Valley Kingston Development, if done according to the plans and presentation of materials reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-64, of the City of Kingston's Administrative Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: - Sign designs are clean and designed to meet the needs but not distract from the historic character of the building or surroundings, having traffic circulation signs meet code and provide basic need to direct and identify uses on site. - One way exit sign will be post mounted, not affixed to building wall. -Signs are designed to provide for more than one user to be accommodated thus, eliminating duplicate or excessive signage. - Any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out. - The Commission's approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; including submission of insurance naming the City as additionally insured as required by Section 358-9 C. of the City Code. Based on the preceding findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 5th day of January 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced applicant/owner, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (MG – motion, RT – 2nd; KM, NM -yes) HAC APPLICATIONS:

items.title: #759 Broadway. New signage for building exterior
items.discussion:
S. Ansbacher was present to discuss the  plan for two new corner signs on Broadway and St
James Pl. The signage company fabricating the signs will be Signarama.  The signs will be made of a plastic-like
vinyl material that is durable in the weather through all seasons. They will be affixed to the wall face with a
masonry bolting mechanism.

Mr. Ansbacher stated there is no plan to have any illumination or window signage on the street.
The signs are planned to be 96in by 42in and face Broadway and Saint James Street. According to Kingston city
Broadway design standards the identifying text should be sized no larger than half the size of the business
name text. This is to protect the size of the signage board. This proposed sign has multiple layers of secondary
text including a website, phone number, and address amounting to much more space than the business name.
After reviewing the regulations, the Commission agreed that the sign follows the Broadway Design Standards
as adopted in the Zoning Code.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the signage as presented for 759 Broadway, on both the Broadway and St. James Street facades. (JM – motion, NM – 2nd, KM, BH – yes)

items.title: #515-517 Wilbur Avenue. Establish new business for light manufacturing - distillery, cannery, tasting room, cocktail lounge, and associated site improvements
items.discussion:
K. Tompkins, W. Tompkins, A. Guzman and J. Niles were present to represent the application.
K. Tomkins began the discussion by giving some background on the company and their experience in the
industry.  The site is a former auto body business, but the location and size are suitable for the business vision
they want.  They are currently operating in West Park and that will remain functioning, this will supplement
and also bring a different component to the business.

S. Cahill reviewed the site improvements planned, including closing up overhead doors along the Wilbur
Avenue face, using a similar architectural block to match the existing structure material.  The new face will
have large windows, with smaller panes and the pavement outside will be replaced with a lawn area.  This
increased green area will not only improve the building aesthetic but will provide for some on-site stormwater
storage.  This face will also have simple lettering to identify the building occupancy, colored with a gray
exterior paint that will also serve to upgrade the appearance of the structure.

A second, wall mounted sign is planned for Greenkill Avenue.  The notation on the plans states that the initial
signage will include board mounted signage attached to the building.  The ultimate intent is to pursue signage
painted directly onto the building façade.  The application states that the total square footage will not exceed
49sf. The details show that the signage will include a “W” & “S” intertwined logo with “Wiltwyck” written
above the logo.  K. Tompkins asked if they chose to reverse colors as shown would there be any issue going
forward.  The Commission discussed both options and agreed that either would be suitable.

An outdoor seating area will be developed adjacent to the building.  This space will be blocked off from the
sidewalk with wooden planter boxes.  K. Tompkins noted they plan to use Belgian block paver stones.  He also
explained that because of the trail adjacent to the site they plan to include bike racks on the property.

S. Cahill noted that along the Kingston Mechanical boundary, there will be a storage container that will
covered to look like it is wood fencing.  The applicants explained that the parking area for the business will be
located in the rear of the building near Wilbur Avenue and will be screened from the street with a wooden
fence and short shrubbery. There will be a total of 15 parking spaces and 1 handicap space on site.  An ADA
accessible ramp will be added for access from the parking lot into the building.  A. Guzman noted that they are
going to use some of the older RR stone blocks to construct the ramp retaining wall component.

Lighting will consist of LED light panels mounted to posts on the building.  They will be 42,000 lumen – 300
watt NextGen III LED Shoebox lights in warm white.  Lighting will be on the rear of the building directed to
the parking lot. Lighting will be on timers turning off 1 hour after closing.  K. Tompkins stated that the
driveway is well lit from the existing streetlights.  They will also have soffit lighting along the street and
outdoor seating wall lighting to illuminate the walls.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and approve the renovation, improvements for the project as presented, noting that if the applicant decides to “flip” colors as discussed, it is approved whether the black, white, or gray as long as it stays grayscale (JM – motion, KM – 2nd, BH, NM– yes)

items.title: #42 Wall Street. Renovations/restoration to an existing house. New exterior porch, gable end roof, and some new windows and doors
items.discussion:
S. Dutton was present to represent the applicants. The parcel in question is a thru lot and has
frontage on both Fair and Wall Streets. The exterior porch is to be constructed alongside a new door on the
first floor of the east side (Fair Street) of the building. The second floor of the east side will receive new double
wide windows. S Dutton remarked that the purpose of these changes are to make the Fair Street entrance read
as the main entrance to the building, even though the address is Wall.

The use is remaining as single family. The south side of the building’s second floor will lose a window as the
plans call for one to be infilled to allow for the establishment of a new bathroom for the master suite. The
western face (Wall Street) will have lattice work removed and new steps installed. Several architectural
features on the inside of the building will be altered as well. Most notably walls and pillars that will be
removed from the first second and third floors.

The gable end roof will be the largest physical alternation to the exterior of the property. It will be on the east
end or Fair Street side, offering new third floor attic storage and will coincide with a roof replacement. All
materials will remain the same. S Dutton remarks that this alteration was almost entirely with aesthetics in
mind. Although it will add some attic space as well for the property owners. S Dutton goes on to say that the

owners are not yet ready to present a new color scheme for the property to the board but that will likely be
coming in the future.

Overall, the existing structure will be given new life with this restoration project. The benefit to the
neighborhood will be welcome. Proposed elevations showing exterior changes proposed.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and approve restoration of 42 Wall (exterior porch, gable roof, windows, landscape) as presented (KM – motion, JM – 2nd, BH, NM – yes)

items.title: #150 Washington Avenue. Home renovation, including new shed dormer on northwest side of building
items.discussion:
S. Dutton was present to represent the applicants. He mentioned the Jordan family purchased
this property like 42 Wall but with a smaller “freshen up” in mind. The principal alteration being a small, shed
dormer just over the stairwell that will raise the ceiling there about three and a half feet to take advantage of
existing attic storage space. S Dutton claims that the alteration will be barely visible from the street unless
you’re coming down Washington Ave but even then, the buildings are close enough together to mask it.  The
Commission agreed that the addition did not significantly alter the appearance of the structure.

S Dutton went on to explain the other alterations of the property will mostly be converting it from a two family
to a one family. The pre-existing second unit was likely not legal according to Dutton but there was a small
kitchen and such on the second floor. Concerns were then raised about landscaping and S Dutton spoke of the
good track record of landscaping the Jordans had.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and approve as presented with exterior dormer, window changes, minor interior reconfigurations (JM – motion, KM – 2nd, BH, NM – yes)

items.title: #59 Pearl Street (aka 236 Wall Street). Renovation of former St. Joseph's School building, adding ten new tenant spaces. Existing assembly space on 3rd floor to remain. New elevator, exterior vestibule, and site modifications for improved ADA accessibility. Replace steam heating system with new high
items.discussion:
S. Dutton was present to represent the applicants.  Discussion started as a history of the
property as the former St Joseph’s school building, when it was purchased by current owner Charles Blaichman
about two years ago, and the previous approval gained for the upper floors by the planning board. The beauty
of the building is also discussed and the effort underway to list it on the national register of historic places.

The principal matter of the meeting on January 5th concerned placement of important HVAC systems and an
elevator. S Dutton claims the age of the building makes placing important modern amenities like these into the

building difficult and that they have exhausted all the possibilities of where to place such systems. Where they
settled was an alleyway north of the building. S Dutton’s architectural plans for the elevator construction are to
make it look modern and not a hide it is a new addition. These plans consist of two to three feet HVAC systems
sitting behind an all-glass elevator vestibule.

Concern is raised by the HAC board that the facilities will eat into a right-of-way for access to the back of both
buildings. S Dutton stated that access would still be available but limited and other options aren’t feasible. The
plans are to make the elevator as inoffensive as possible while still making the space comply with ADA code. S
Dutton remarks that they’ll still need to gain the approval of New York State, the national park service, and
SHPO. The sizes and dimensions of the new elevator will pass regulation when the doors are open, maintaining
a five-foot radius circle. Much of the plans were drawn up by an elevator expert out of New York City due to
the complexity of the design.

Some discussion was made concerning private efforts and next steps to place the building in a neighboring
historic district before the motions were made to approve the project.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve as presented for vestibules and elevator addition and condenser units. (KM – motion, JM – 2nd, NM, BH – yes) Next Joint Meeting: February 2, 2023 This meeting will be live-streamed at the City of Kingston YouTube channel: https://www.youtube.com/c/CityofKingstonNY

items.title: HAC Adoption of the Minutes of January 5, 2023 Meeting. HLPC Adoption of the Minutes of January 5, 2023 Meeting

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to adopt the minutes from the January 5, 2023 meeting. (JM – motion, NM – 2nd, BH – yes)
A. Puetz recused herself from voting because she was not present at the previous meeting. The Commission did not have a quorum to vote. HLPC BUSINESS:

items.title: Form Based Zoning Code DISCUSSION on setting a special workshop meeting for the Historic Landmarks Preservation Commission to review and prepare comment back to the Common Council on the proposed City-wide Form Based Zoning Code
items.discussion:
The HLPC discussed potential meeting dates for a special workshop to provide recommendations
to the Common Council on the proposed city-wide Form Based Zoning Code. The Commission agreed to hold
a meeting on February 9, 2023 at 6:30 PM.  Staff will provide sections of the document to review, but the entire
proposed code is at www.engagekingston.com  M. Grunblatt noted that he believes there are discrepancies
with other sections of the Code which should be cleaned up and made consistent.  S. Cahill noted that the
HLPC would be reviewing only the zoning area, but if there are inconsistencies, they can be identified and
noted for addition code updating by the Council under a separate action.  S. Cahill also stated that although the
referral is for the HLPC, the members of the HAC will be included on the invite and welcome to participate.
The workshop will be in-person and open to public.
HAC/HLPC JOINT REGULAR BUSINESS:

items.title: #311 Wall Street Install sign along Wall Street, on 2nd floor of building, and signage on the Crown Street face of building. Add 4, 10’x10’ overhead glass/alum. Doors to Crown Street. Related site work such as, landscaping, lighting, storm drainage
items.discussion:
Paul Jankovitz, Architect; and Corbin Plays, applicant’s representative; were present at the
meeting.  They explained that they were returning to the Board after being tabled at the January 2023 meeting.
They distributed an updated plan sheet with details of the rear awning on Crown Street.   C. Plays presented
the awning material to the Commissions.  The material is Sunbrella fabric in Erin Green 4600-0000.  This was
information that was requested by the Commissions.  All agreed that it was suitable.

P. Jankovitz stated that he had already provided to staff some documentation outlining the archeological
procedures for discovery and documentation, along with the credentials of the Archeology Firm to be employed
for purposes of all excavation monitoring. The architectural firm, Hudson Cultural Services, provided the
qualifications for the lead archeologist that will be working on the project and background on the firm,
identifying experience with various projects and programs, along with familiarity with regulations and
practices.  Also submitted was a map showing the proposed test pits for archeological monitoring including the
dry well locations and the test trenches for the former building footprint and  an “Archeological Monitoring
Report 311 Wall Street Parking Lot Rehabilitation” dated January 2023.

S. Cahill noted that P. Jankovitz had been in the Planning Office to review additional materials in the files.  It
was noted that the archeology firm should review the information from the Planning Department files, with
regard to the buildings that fronted on Crown Street and were demolished on the site.  This information may
result in modifications to the plans for the excavation and trenching.

The monitoring plan submitted lays out the following information: Project Description, Archeological
Methods, Archeological Monitoring Essential Elements, Monitoring Report, Contractor Responsibilities,
Archeologist Responsibilities, Human Remains Protocol, References. Staff noted that there may be adjustments
in the field when work is underway.  These could be reviewed and approved with staff to avoid work delay.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to support the HLPC’s Preservation Notice of Action approving the application. (JM – motion, NM – 2nd, BH – yes)

The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed renovations and restoration at 311 Wall Street, in the Stockade Historic District, by applicant 311 Wall Street LLC, if done according to the plans and presentation of materials reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-64, of the City of Kingston’s Administrative Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: - The Wall Street facade will remain largely intact, with new lettering to reflect the historic character of the previous “Woolworth” signage, with individual letters, measuring 3’x3’, LED backlit, constructed with metal base with chrome finish and cast resin lettering face, color to match historic red. The individual lettering will spell out “Kingston Studios” with a total length of 60’. Signage for future tenants in the Wall Street retail spaces will return to the HLPC for review and approval under the existing guidelines of the Pike Plan. - Crown Street signage will include lettering depicting “No. 311”. The signage will be 4’1”x 21’10 and will be backlit, post-mounted to the brick with masonry anchors. The lettering will be sheet metal with chrome finish. An awning will also be added over the rear entrance printed with “Kingston Studios”, using Sunbrella canvas product in Erin Green #4600-0000. - Hudson Cultural Services Ltd. (HCS), under the leadership of Beth Selig, MA, RPA, who will be the Professional Archaeologist overseeing work and responsible for a qualified archaeologist to be present on site during any and all excavation activity. The submitted a plan for work including a map for excavation, and a plan for inventory, cataloging and documentation and retention of unearthed materials and artifacts, scope of work and plan for action if significant artifact is discovered, is hereby accepted and will be strictly adhered to at all times; and may be modified as site conditions dictate, with staff approval. - The parking area contains two locations specified for food trucks. These spaces will be occupied in coordination with special events and are not intended to be permanent locations or for the general public. No outside seating is proposed. - Landscaping will be added to the rear parking area with locations and species finalized with the Planning Board site plan review. - Any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out. - The Commission’s approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston’s Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies. Based on the preceding findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 2nd day of February 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced applicant/owner, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (MG – motion, AP – 2nd, NM, RT – yes)

items.title: #71 Abeel Street. Removal and addition of windows and replacement of a front door, stabilization work on structure
items.discussion:
The architect, Jesse Meisler Abramson was present at the meeting. He explained that the
application is for replacement of windows and doors and stabilization work on an existing structure in the
Rondout District. He noted  that the current windows are already vinyl replacement, and not at all historic.
They are proposing to install manufactured wooden windows, specified as Anderson A-Series Low E2 w/
Argon, exterior color white, interior clear coat pine, all hardware in matte white. The doors will be Low 2E
with Argon, exterior white, interior clear coat pine, all hardware in matte white.

Three windows will be double hung 6 over 6; one will be double hung not divided; 2 will be casement style
with 12 panes; one will be single casement under the roof overhang, and 2 will be casement with 9 panes.
Although not visible from the street, in the rear a window will replace a second story doorway.  The front door
will have glass panels and side glass panels.  The rear doors will be glass sliders.

The Commissions reviewed the plans, comparing the proposed work using both the existing photos provided,
but also using an older image taken from historic records.  It was noted that the planned improvements would
be inline with efforts to upgrade the property and appropriately undertake restoration.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to support the HLPC’s Preservation Notice of Action approving the application. (NM – motion, JM – 2nd, BH – yes)

The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed window and door replacement and the stabilization work at 71 Abeel Street, in the Rondout Historic District, by applicant Alex Kahn and Florian Doumenc, if done according to the plans and presentation of materials reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405- 64, of the City of Kingston’s Administrative Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: - The owners are replacing the existing vinyl windows with Anderson A-Series Low E2 in exterior white and interior clear coat pine. Three windows will be double hung 6 over 6, one double hung not divided, 2 casement with 12 panes, 2 casement with 9 panes, and 1 single casement under the roof overhang. - The front door will be Simpson F-37944U-W with 9 panel glass and side light panels. The rear door will be an Anderson Slide 4 Panel. - Any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out. - The Commission’s approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston’s Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies. Based on the preceding findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 2nd day of February 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced applicant/owner, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (MG – motion, NM – 2nd, AP, RT – yes)

items.title: #93 Fair Street Amendment to approved plan to replace existing windows
items.discussion:
R. Arket was present to discuss the current plans for renovation, which amend what had
previously been presented and approved by the Commissions.    Since the Preservation Notice was adopted in
December 2022, he has begun renovations to the structure.  After removing the windows with the intentions of
restoring them, they have determined that to be cost prohibitive and are now looking to  request permission to
replace all of the windows.

The windows proposed are Pella Reserve aluminum clad wood windows in black.  They will be double hung 6
over 6 to replicate the original wood windows.  There will be no changes in dimensions or locations of
openings.  All windows will remain with no closures or infill.

The applicant submitted  a PowerPoint with the details which the Commission reviewed.  It documented
minimal conditions, but di demonstrate cleaning and work that ad been done.  One photo was referenced to
identify the location of a second chimney in the center of the structure that is also being requested to be
removed.  R. Arket noted that it is not needed and stated that it along with the side chimney on Fair Street
(already approved) would both be removed, allowing for extra interior space and also cleaning up the outer
appearance.

Staff prepared an amended Preservation Notice of Action for consideration.

The application is can be considered a Type II action under SEQR and therefore is predetermined to have no
significant environmental impact and no further review of the Commissions are required.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to support the HLPC’s Preservation Notice of Action approving the application. (NM – motion, JM – 2nd, BH – yes)

The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed renovations and restoration at 93 Fair Street, in the Fair Street Historic District, by applicant Ryan Arket, if done according to the plans and presentation of materials reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-64, of the City of Kingston’s Administrative Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: - The existing stucco will be repaired and painted with Benjamin Moore - Woodlawn Blue HC-147. - The existing windows will be replaced with Pella Reserve aluminum clad, wood windows in black. - The existing chimneys, one central to structure, and the second facing Fair Street will both be removed, bringing back the original facade, new rounded gutters will be added, and the existing aluminum fascia will be painted Benjamin Moore Hale Navy HC-154. - The roof will replaced with GAF Timberline Natural Shadow Charcoal Architectural Shingles. - The exterior doors and garage door will be painted in Benjamin Moore Hale Navy HC-154. - Any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out. - The Commission's approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies. Based on the amended preceding findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 2nd day of February 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced applicant/owner, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (MG – motion, AP – 2nd, RT, NM – yes)

items.title: #5 Abeel Street, 8 & 10 Post Street Modifications for exterior renovations to an existing building
items.discussion:
No one was present at the meeting.  A. Puetz recused herself from the discussion based on her
employment with the applicant.  Staff noted that S. Dutton, representing the owner, was aware of the lack of
quorum and agreed to have the project tabled for a month.

decisions.text: The application was tabled due to the lack of a quorum; the application will be added to the March 2023 agenda.
There was no vote on the application; it will be added to the March 2023 agenda. HAC APPLICATIONS:

items.title: #693-701 Broadway. Proposal to demolish freestanding garage structure and establish open green space
items.discussion:
The applicants were not present at the meeting.  S. Cahill explained that the Commission
previously approved the application to demolish the building and rebuild a similar building in its place.  The
structure was previously occupied as a motor vehicle service station.  It has remained vacant for a period of
time.  The applicants are now requesting approval to still demolish the building, but create an open green
space. S. Cahill asked that if the Commission is favorable to the new plan, that they also consider allowing the
landscaping elements and final details to be worked out with planning staff rather than returning to the
Commission.  The Commission welcomed the addition of more greenspace along the Broadway corridor,
encouraging the use of a variety of plantings, including native species and permeable paving techniques. It was
noted that no lighting was presented with the plans.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously issue a negative declaration of environmental significance under SEQR and to approve the application to demolish the garage building and to allow the landscaping and lighting details to be approved by staff. (JM – motion, NM – 2nd, BH – yes)

items.title: #541-545 Broadway (537 Broadway) Install freestanding sign with a 96” width and 24” height. Painted PVC panel with 58” width and 12.25” height PVC letters applied
items.discussion:
Tyson McCasland, Timely Signs, was present at the meeting.  He explained that the application is
to install a double-sided freestanding sign to identify an existing business. The business, formerly known as
Ulster Uniform, is now known as “UniFirst” and is the same type of business, just under a new name.  The sign
will be 96” wide x 24” high with white, routed, PVC lettering measuring 58”W x 12.25” H x 5” thick.

The applicant was asked if there was any consideration to landscaping around the base or any lighting.  T.
McCasland said that the owners are only interested in replacing the sign face and that the location is difficult
to access for landscaping or excavating for lighting.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application for new signage. (JM – motion, NM – 2nd, BH – motion)

items.title: #484 Broadway Install a street facing sign with dimensions of 12’ by 4’ using pre-existing sign frame and illumination, install LED borders for the two front most facing window spaces 53” by 77” and 81” by 77”, and add LED sign in the 41” by 77” window directly adjacent to the door at a size of 33.0

items.applicant: Robert Hunt, Jason Van Aken, Gregory Lodato
items.discussion:
Jason Van Aken was present at the meeting.  He explained that he is one third of a partnership
opening a tattoo parlor in an existing building on Broadway.  The applicants are proposing to install new
business identification signage for a tattoo business opening in an existing storefront space.

The Commission reviewed the information submitted including a mockup of the signage on the building.  The
wall sign will be located in the existing sign location and will be the same size and shape as the previous
signage.  The existing gooseneck style lights will be used to illuminate the sign.  The sign will be hand painted
graphics with enamel sign paint onto sheet metal.  The sign will measure 12’ wide x 4’ high.

Signage also includes an LED eagle symbol to be hung within the building and shown through the window.
The eagle will be approximately 5.5 feet tall and 2.5 feet wide.  The bird graphic will be yellow with a red
sunburst behind.  The windows will have an LED blue surrounding light with window graphics spelling out
“Skin City North” “As ancient as time… as modern as tomorrow”.  The door will have the name, phone number
and hours of operation.

Catarina Cowden was present at the meeting.  She explained that she is seeking approval to install
an overhanging sign on an existing building.  She said that the small space is somewhat hidden because it is
part of another building and is not visible.  The sign will hang perpendicular to the street over the public right
of way.  The applicant was advised that insurance naming the City as additionally insured will need to be
obtained and submitted.

C. Cowden noted that sign presently sits in the window by the doorway.  It is hand painted with a cream
background and terracotta writing stating “The Little Rye Bake House”, measuring 15”x24”.  They plan to hang
it from a 24” bracket attached to the building with eyehooks to hang the sign.

The applicant told the Commission that she is currently only open for retail one day a week on Sundays, 10am-
2pm.  At present. She is the only employee of the business and operates as a wholesale business most of the

time.  She may expand her retail hours in the future, noting that already there are “regulars” stopping in on
Sundays.

The applicants were not present at the meeting.  S. Cahill explained that the NYS DEC
determined the action to be a Type II action under SEQR and that the Coastal Consistency review is not
required for Type II actions.

(Note: This item was reviewed at the beginning of the meeting at the request of the applicant).
Peter and Marta Dvorak were present at the meeting.  They explained that the are seeking approval to install 5
new windows in an existing structure, with only 4 visible from street. The windows are located on the side of
the building, and one in the rear.  One window towards the back will be reduced in size.  The applicants
explained that they were unaware that they needed review by the HAC and had already begun to install the
new windows.  The reason for the replacement is for efficiency and because some of the existing windows did
not open.  The Commission asked about the other windows in the building. The applicants said that the other
windows appeared to be newer and that these 5 windows were probably not replaced because there was a
tenant that resided in the space for 25+ years.  S. Cahill added that the owners are not replacing the windows in
the front of the house that have the stained glass details.  Those windows will remain.

All of the windows are white, vinyl, double hung windows.  They are energy star rated by Dor-Win
Manufacturing.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the proposed signage as submitted. (JM – motion, NM – 2nd, BH – yes) 10. #588 Broadway Installation of a 15” by 24” sign hung perpendicular to the building using a bracket. SBL 56.25-3-26.200. SEQR Type II. Zone C-2, Midtown mixed HA.
