items.title: # 12 Warren Street. Installation of 8 solar panels on existing roof totaling 2.96kw
items.discussion:
The applicant was not present.  The project is to install eight Prexos Series 8 PV panels on the
structure’s second story southwest facing roof, with the front 6 being visible from Warren Street, and two
additional PV panels will be installed on the southeast facing roof of the rear porch (not visible from the
street). SnapNrack mounts and umbrella screws (into the rafters) will be used to mount the panels to the
asphalt roof. The use of flash track indicates the panels will align with rafters of the primary roof (AR-01)’s
current 47-degree pitch and the secondary rear porch roof (AR-02)’s 4-degree pitch. The applicant has also
submitted the NY State Unified Solar Permit application.

Mighty Engineering Co.’s structural evaluation of the structure’s roof and the PV module indicates that
the scope of the work complies with local building provisions. Paul Joyce of Sunrun Installation Services
Inc. will serve as the project’s installer and electrician, and the applicant has submitted his credentials and
the necessary local and state permits.
PV interconnection or junction box will be located on the east face of the structure, facing the rear of
153 Wall Street. Staff recommended that electrical lines match the structure’s exterior color (white) and if
necessary be obscured from street view by white lattice.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application as presented. (NM-motion, MD-2nd, BH, JM, KM – yes)

items.title: #47 German Street. Installation of 4 new windows. Foundation water barrier, and repair to woodwork and painting
items.applicant: German Street, LLC c/o Miguel Alvarado
items.owner: German Street, LLC c/o Miguel Alvarado
items.discussion:
The applicant/owner, Miguel Alvarado, was not present, and his wife Kristen Wilson,
represented their project. Staff noted that the building lies just outside of the historic district boundary,
only in the HAC area, but does have an impact on the district as adjacent property.  The Commission
reviewed the following issues with K. Wilson:
• They are seeking to install 4 new black Anderson 400 windows, in a 6 over 1 pattern (see attached
specifications) on the ground floor along Ravine and German Streets where the current windows are
boarded because of damage. The applicant began the installation of these windows not realizing he
needed approval and was halted before the project’s completion by the city’s inspectors. These
windows are intended to replace the existing, non-original, and damaged windows but will be black
instead of matching the structure’s beige/yellow paint. The applicant will submit a comprehensive plan
later this year drafted by an architect which will include the replacement of additional windows across
the structure with the same black Anderson 400 windows and painting the third story windows black.
Staff noted that the project also includes repairing the German Street ground floor entrance’s wooden
landing with similar materials and; to repair and paint in the same color (creamy/yellow), the German
Street porch which shows signs of water damage.
• They are also seeking approval to install a water barrier on the northwest (uphill) foundation’s exterior
to halt and prevent future water infiltration. M. Alvarado had previously clarified with the staff that
waterproofing will be done on structure’s exterior along the uphill side, and partially along the 49
German Street side, but not on the Ravine Street Side. The plan includes excavating a trench
approximately 4 feet wide from the foundation and down to its base to create a French drain. K.
Wilson acknowledged that they are aware  that excavation within the Heritage Area requires a degree
of sensitivity. To this, they agree to notify the Planning Department in the event any cultural or
archaeological materials are unearthed.
• Staff noted that although it does not appear that any work will take place in the public ROW, the
applicant is advised to get a permit from DPW if any work or disturbance take place within the public
right-of-way, including any blocking of the sidewalk with the movement or storage of materials.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application as presented, noting that the conditions which are outlined within the discussion: 1) Submission of comprehensive plan for exterior renovations before additional work is performed. 2) Notification of City Planning Office if any archeological or other materials are exposed during excavation so that items will not be destroyed. 3) Obtain permit from DPW for any blocking, disturbance, or other work within the public right-of-way. (NM-motion, JM-2nd, KM, BH, MD - yes)

items.title: #50 Crane St. Replacing windows, roof, siding, and rebuilding porch and soffits. Foundation issues will be rectified as needed
items.discussion:
Noe Del Cid, representing RUPCO was present.  RUPCO, in partnership with the City of
Kingston, and funded by Health Alliance Hospital, Homes and Community Renewal of New York State and
other funding sources; is taking on the task of rehabbing this home to modern and high efficiency standards
and selling the home to a low-income buyer at 60% below area median income. The applicant states that all
1/1 windows will be replaced with a single light high performance casement window.
The Commission discussed the change in the second-floor window configuration and encouraged
retaining the separation of the two windows to maintain the outward architectural integrity.  Staff noted
the on-going project under the CLG Program which is looking at all properties in this area for potential
eligibility to be historically recognized.  N. Del Cid stated that they intended to install a triple window on
the second story connecting the north and central windows but will remove this from the plans. A triple
window on the first floor by the porch will remain within the project’s scope.
The applicant also clarified that they intend to keep and restore the single multicolored window
beneath the street facing gable, the roof will be replaced with gray asphalt shingles, and the proposed
foundation work will be visible, but repairs will be done with like materials to ensure no significant
changes to its appearance. The structure will be clad in Deep Ocean Blue Hardie Board siding. The porch
and soffits will be restored in kind.  Minor landscaping of the yard area is also planned.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application as presented with change. (JM-motion, MD-2nd, BH, KM, NM – yes) HAC/HLPC JOINT REGULAR BUSINESS:

items.title: #95 Wurts Street House renovations 2 apartment units with heat and A.C. one of which is visible from the street
items.discussion:
P. Benkert was present.  He explained to the Commissions the proposal to paint and add
mechanicals to the building while also conducting restoration work. The applicant agreed to install fencing
or a 2’x2’ planter box with arborvitae (Evergreen bush) to shield the exterior HVAC condenser unit from
view. The lines from the exterior unit will be treated to match the exterior paint color so that they are
blended and less obvious from view.  P. Benkert noted that he would also like to replace the bluestone
pathway on their property with concrete dyed and textured to mimic a bluestone appearance. Staff noted

that the public sidewalk condition is in disrepair, and that the applicant should use the bluestone taken up
on site to  to repair the sidewalk, with a DPW permit approval. P. Benkert agreed to follow this directive.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed installation of heat pumps at 95 Wurts Street, in the Rondout Historic District, by the owner Paul Benkert, if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-64, of the City of Kingston's Administrative Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: • NYS SHPO holds a Building-Structure Form for 95 Wurts St created by the Friends of Historic Kingston in October of 1976 and states the following: "This Second Empire residence appears on the 1870 Beers map of Rondout. Judging from the 1858 French map, it replaced an earlier structure. It retains its original 19th-century features and has received no major modern alterations. It is one of the more notable residences of its style in the district"; • This work will cause a material change to the external appearance of the property and in doing so will aid in restoring and preserving the structure; • There is only one small unit mounted on the side and setback from the roadway making it minimally visible from the street; • The applicant will provide planter box 2'x2' arborvitae (Evergreen) to assist with screening the installation from view; • The pipe casing will be treated to match the existing exterior color of the main structure; -The applicant will replace broken bluestone pathway along the dwelling's south side with stamped concrete dyed to match the original bluestone; - The applicant will use existing on-site bluestone being removed from on-site pathway to repair the bluestone public sidewalk and will secure a DPW permit; • Any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; • The Commission's approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 6th day of April 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (MG-motioned, RT-2nd, KM, NM, AP – yes)

The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application as presented and endorse the Preservation Notice of Action as adopted by the HLPC. (NM-motion, MD-2nd, BH, KM, JM – yes)

items.title: #5 Abeel Street, 8 & 10 Post Street Modifications for exterior renovations to an existing building
items.discussion:
NOTE: Andrea Puetz recused herself from the HLPC Commission as an employee of SDA, and
she served as a representative for both S. Dutton Associates and the owner. Andrea gave the following

presentation:
1. The foremost discovery is a subterranean room suspected to have been a root cellar or storage area to
the rear (north) of the structure. During the initial survey of the structure, this room was missed
entirely as its access was blocked in by a concrete masonry wall. Demolition of this wall while shoring
up the structure revealed this space. It has not caved in and holds firm despite the multitude of
structural complications around the site. We are including the cellar as a part of the submission; it shall
be made free of debris, its vaulted brick ceiling and stone foundation walls cleaned and repointed as per
NPS preservation briefings, and a new concrete slab poured on the floor, as it is currently dirt. It will be
kept as a storage space, since there is no fenestration present, and the ceiling is too low to be a usable
space.
2. On the Abeel St façade, the roof deck that appears on the first floor will no longer be a balcony, but roof
only. Structurally, the rafters were never meant to hold the weight required to be a roof deck. The
roofing material will be replaced with EPDM (rubber) and the guard rail removed. The door that
accesses the roof deck will be replaced with a window, and the space below the window will be infilled
with new siding milled to match the surrounding clapboard.
3. Windows: All windows are to be replaced with new wood windows (same as previously submitted),
however grille or muntin patterns are to change as follows: a. Abeel St wing (southeast face): All double
hung windows are to be 9/9 instead of 6/6, except the single casement window (with simulated check
rail to appear as a double hung window) on second floor - this shall remain 6/6. b. Post St wing
(southwest face): All double hung windows are to be 9/9 instead of 6/6. The second-floor picture
windows will have the wood lattice removed, and a 6 lite grille is to be installed. c. Post St wing
(northwest face): First floor double hung window to remain 6/6, second floor casement window (with
simulated check rail to appear as a double hung window) also to remain 6/6 d. Post St wing (northeast
face): No windows will have a grille pattern as they were modern additions. A new dormer (to be
discussed in another section) will have the same style windows as on the southwest face. e. Abeel St
wing (northwest face): The lone double hung window to be 9/9 instead of 6/6
4. Doors; all exterior: All exterior doors are to be retained and restored, including the door accessing the
main mercantile space from Abeel St (it will be carefully removed, scraped, patched, repaired, and
reinstalled after the new storefront system has been installed).
5. Porch on Post St wing, northeast face: The porch will be removed in entirety as it is not an historic
aspect of the structure. A new sloped roof canopy with asphalt shingle will shelter the existing door,
and a bluestone slab landing will be installed.
6. New dormer on Post St wing, northeast face: A new dormer will be added to the second floor to
improve head room at the top of the stairs and access into the two bedrooms. It will also include (3)
new picture windows. Its visible impact is minimal from both Abeel and Post streets since it is on the
rear of the structure.
7. Roof extension and deck on rear of Abeel St wing, northwest face: A new larger deck is to be built
over top of the rear mechanical area and partially over the brick vaulted storage area, and a new roof is
to extend out over only the mechanical room portion of the deck. The new roof will be EPDM due to its
low slope.

items.title: Existing porch to apartment on Post St wing, southwest face: The porch and its roof structure (new EPDM installed) are to remain and be restored and a new stair, hand and guard rail are to be installed as previously proposed. However, the area under the stairs is to be opened and a new low height re

One space in question sits directly over top of the cellar, and for safety reasons should be removed. The space will become a part of the graded grass area instead. The acc

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed amendments to the renovation and restoration, at 5 Abeel Street and 8&10 Post Street, and parking lot, in the Rondout Historic District, by the owner CBSKI Kingston LLC (Charles Blaichman), if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-64, of the City of Kingston’s Administrative Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: • that the proposed work is to take place at these five bays, 1.5 story circa 1850 house with a gable roof running parallel to Post Street and which appears on the 1858 J.H. French map of Ulster County; • This work will cause a material change to the external appearance of the property and in doing so will aid in restoring and preserving the structure; • The asphalt siding will be removed, wood clapboard siding will be either restored or replaced, if necessary, wood details and trim will be restored and painted, the ground floor storefront will be renovated, new storefront windows will be added, new wood windows will replace deteriorated and missing windows, brick will be cleaned and re-pointed. • New windows will include 9/9 and 6/6 on the Abeel and Post Street facades as per plans submitted. The grill patterns on the second story Post Street windows will be removed. Doors will be retained and restored. The porch on the Post Street wing will be removed and a new sloped roof canopy with asphalt shingles will be added above the door and a bluestone slab landing will be installed. • Due to structural issues, the roof deck balcony along the Abeel Street facade will no longer be a balcony but will be a roof only. The roof will be EPDM rubber and the handrail feature removed. The second- floor door to access will now be a window and the space surrounding will be filled with new siding to match. • A new dormer will be added to the second story on the Post Street wing to improve head room at the top of the stairs and access into two bedrooms. It will also include 3 new picture windows. A new larger deck and roof covering will be added in the rear of the Abeel Street wing. The area under the Post wing porch will be opened and a new low height retaining wall will be built around the perimeter of the porch. Porch columns will rest on the retaining wall. • The Commission recognizes a lot line deletion will need to be approved by the Planning Board and filed with the County for final occupancy or required cross-easements will need to be provided and approved by Corporation Counsel prior to signature for filing. • The structure will be painted Benjamin Moore White Winged Dove - 1457, with white trim. • Any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; • The Commission’s approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 6th day of April 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. items.title: # 18 W Union Street. Removal of an enclosed porch, construct new 208sf addition to 1st floor. Adding a second story with shed dormers. Replacing aluminum siding with composite clapboard, window, and door replacement. Addition of 96 sf balcony on the structure’s rear. Project includes additional apar
items.discussion:
Scott P. Roeber, R.A. of Hudson Valley Architecture, LLC and John Stewart (owner) presented
on their proposed work at 18 West Union St:
• S. Roeber explained that the applicant seeks to build an addition to West Union Street facing the side
of their structure (6.5’x32’) which will expand the dwelling’s first floor space by approximately 208
sq/ft. To accomplish this, the applicant will remove a West Union Street facing, enclosed porch, which
currently features a centralized doorway flanked by four 1/1 windows on either side. The proposed
work will result in a centralized doorway with side lights flanked by three 6/6 windows on the east
(left) and two 6/6/ windows on the west (right side).  The first floor of the existing house will be re-
configured on the interior to create and new kitchen, living area, laundry room and bedroom.  It is
noted that the chimney is being removed, so it is presumed the heating system will be completely
removed also.   Three new heat pump/condenser units are being placed along the walkway on the south
elevation.
• The owner also wants to add a second story to the dwelling with a single gable combination roof
oriented lengthwise towards Post Street. The structure will feature two shed dormers on either side of
the roof, with the Union Street dormer featuring a centralized 9 pane window flanked by a pair of 9
pane windows on either side. All existing windows will be replaced during this project with pebble
gray Marvin Elevate series double-hung casement windows (specs unknown), and the roof will be
replaced with a LOKSEAM Zip System 16” width black/gray standing seam roof.  The second story will
serve as a master bedroom suite for the owner.
• Once interior reconfiguration and new construction is complete, the aluminum siding will be replaced
with white Hardieboard clapboard siding. Neighboring properties are predominantly brick
construction; however, clapboard siding is consistent within this district’s streetscapes. Commissioner
McEvoy noted that on CRIS, this structure is not deemed to be contributing to the historic district as
it presently exists.
• A new 8x12’ elevated deck will be constructed on the east face of the building that will be visible from
West Union Street and Post Street. The retaining wall currently under construction will have steps
that will feature vegetation to balance the massive stonework at the property’s southeastern public
facing corner.
• The project includes adding a second residential unit in the lower level.  This will have separate access
from the east and will be a new one-bedroom unit.  The existing stairs on the north are being re-built
to provide one exterior entry pathway, the staircase and existing walkway to the south will remain the
same.  The Planning Board will be reviewing this project as a site plan.  Other site related features will
also be evaluated with the plan (stormwater, parking, lighting, refuse/recycling storage and location,
etc.)

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed rehabilitation, first and second story additions, the addition of a balcony on the structure's rear, and the creation of an additional apartment unit in the basement level at 18 West Union Street, in the Rondout Historic District, by the applicant Hudson Valley Architecture, LLC. and the owner John Stewart, if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-64, of the City of Kingston's Administrative Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: • that the proposed work is to take place at the one and a half store mid-20th-century house, at the southeastern corner of West Union and Post Street, where according to the 1870 Beers map previously stood a Synagogue; • This work will cause a material change to the external appearance of the property and in doing so will aid in restoring and preserving the structure; • The proposal will include an addition to West Union Street facing the side of their structure (6.5'x32') which will expand the dwelling's first floor space by approximately 208 sq/ft. To accomplish this, the applicant will remove a West Union Street facing, enclosed porch, which currently features a centralized doorway flanked by four 1/1 windows on either side. The proposed work will result in a centralized doorway with side lights flanked by three 12 pane casement windows on the east (left) and two 6/6/ windows on the west (right side). The first floor of the existing house will be re-configured on the interior to create and new kitchen, living area, laundry room and bedroom. It is noted that the chimney is being removed and three new heat pump/condenser units are being placed along the walkway on the south elevation. Any exterior line sets will be treated to match the exterior color of the structure; • A second story will be added to the dwelling with a single gable combination roof oriented lengthwise towards Post Street. The structure will feature two shed dormers on either side of the roof, with the Union Street dormer featuring a centralized 9 pane window flanked by a pair of 9 pane windows on either side; • Other exterior upgrades/installations include replacing all existing windows with pebble gray Marvin Elevate series double-hung casement windows, installing a new roof with a LOKSEAM Zip System 16” width black/gray standing seam roof, and using white Hardieboard for the exterior finish: • A new 8x12' elevated deck will be constructed on the east face of the building that will be visible from West Union Street and Post Street, and adhere to the six-foot set back required in this neighborhood; • Other site elements that will be refreshed include new landscaping in tiered retaining walls and continued stonework on face of all streets facing retaining wall areas; • Any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; • The Commission's approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 6th day of April 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (MG-motion, RT-2nd, AP, NM, KM - yes)

The Commission Voted Unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application as presented and endorse the Preservation Notice of Action as adopted by the HLPC. (MD-motion, NM-2nd, BH, KM, JM-yes)

items.title: #100 Wurts St. Installation of signage, window replacement, front step and door restoration, HVAC installation, and painting front door and window shutters
items.discussion:
A. Wright, Architect and Gary Heckelman, Project Manager were present.  The applicant is
working with Andrew Wright of Wright Architect’s PLLC to replace and modify the structure’s windows
along with other minor exterior alterations/additions.  The plans show 4 categories of window work, keyed
to the elevation plans.  New windows are being proposed as vinyl 6/1.  Most neighboring structures on
Wurts Street also display 6/1 windows. After discussing the replacement project, the Commissions
requested, and the owner’s representative and architect agreed that all the wooden windows on along the
Wurts Street side be restored rather than replaced with vinyl. The side windows were allowed to be
replaced due to heavy screening and no visual impact.
All the structure’s shutters are being restored and will be repainted at the same time using Benjamin
Moore Essex Green HC-188 (samples provided). This is a darker green than what the shutters are currently
painted. The applicant stated the existing shutters are made of wood.
The applicant also plans to repaint the front door using Benjamin Moore Classic Burgundy HC-182.
The applicant also seeks the approval for a 7” circular sign affixed to the front portico’s column (already
installed).  A. Wright stated that the front single step replacement was modified  with two steps and safety
railings to comply with NYS codes, without review. It is shown in the submission that the front entry has
been reconstructed, using a bluestone material to match the pre-existing, but now it has an additional step
and wrought iron handrails have been added to meet Code.  Photographs of this work before and after have
been submitted.  Although it is a visual change, much of the original material is retained and the change
does not negatively impact the structure’s integrity.
Lastly, the applicant is seeking approval for the installation of a heat-pump compressor unit atop the
driveway’s portico entryway (already installed without review) and an enclosure composed of a white
wooden lattice to obscure the unit from view (not installed).

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed installation of signage, window replacement, front step and door restoration, HVAC installation, and front door and window shutter painting at 100 Wurts Street, in the Rondout Historic District, by the owner Circle of Friends for the Dying, Inc., if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-64, of the City of Kingston's Administrative Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: • that the proposed work is to take place at the 2.5 story residence on the northeast side on Wurst St between Rogers St and W. Pierpoint St, dating to circa 1850 and which is present on the 1858 French and 1870 Beers Maps of the area, and which was renovated in the mid-20th-century to conform with the Colonial Revival style; • This work will cause a material change to the external appearance of the property and in doing so will aid in restoring and preserving the structure; • Only the side and rear windows will be replaced with new vinyl 6/1 windows consistent with the structure's current style and neighboring structures, and the shutters will be repaired and repainted in Benjamin Moore Essex Green HC-188; • No work will be done to the Wurts Street facing windows without returning back to the HLPC for review; • The front entryway door will be painted Benjamin Moore Classic Burgundy HC-182; • The Wurts Street entry has been re-set with additional step, constructed of bluestone materials to match existing and new safety, metal handrails are installed; • A heat-pump condenser unit is located atop the driveways portico entryway and will be screened by white lattice; • Installation of a 7" circular sign affixed to the front portico's column will identify the building name and occupancy; • Any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; • The Commission's approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 6th day of April 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (MG-motion, RT-2nd, KM, AP, NM - yes)

The Commission Voted Unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application as presented and endorse the Preservation Notice of Action as adopted by the HLPC. (JM-motion, MD-2nd, BH, JM, KM - yes)

items.title: #89 John Street. Repairing and replacing wooden features in-kind, repairing brick and mortar in-kind, repainting the structure, replacing exterior light fixtures, creation of a patio area with raised planting bed in front yard, and installation of wrought iron flower boxes beneath second story windo

items.discussion:
Dara Trahan and Dr. Lippert were present.  D. Trahan reviewed the proposal submitted before
the Commissions.  They had prepared a detailed narrative explaining the work they propose to undertake
at their property to repair and repaint exterior elements at 89 John Street. She reviewed the proposed scope
of work as follows:
• Scrape off peeling paint, wash exterior, repoint brick were needed.
• Fix and caulk rotted wood trim, soffits, fascia board and box gutter sheaths.
• Prime exterior then paint the facades with Sherwin Williams colors.
• Switch out brass/gold tone wall lanterns (front door) with black carriage lanterns.
• Add wrought iron flower boxes to 3 windows on second level and to farthest window from street on
first level (front elevation).
• Replant existing raised bed.
• Add small brick patio area and matching raised bed to recessed area in front.

• Replace cracked side alley door & one broken rear window.
• No changes to building footprint or height are planned.

The Commission’s noted that 89 John Street is a 1925, 2-story, brick townhouse style structure. It was
formerly used for residential purposes, including as living quarters for firemen, before being converted to
commercial use. The second level has been transformed into living space for the building owners, Dr.
Lippert & his wife.
D. Trahan noted that around 1996, Dr. Lippert appeared before the Commission to repaint the building.
The Commission steered Dr. Lippert away from his proposed yellow palette and recommended the blue
scheme currently on the structure. The building’s brick facade is now in need of repair and repainting with
the northwest corner showing the most paint loss. Many of the wooden elements also need repair and the
front exterior lighting is weathered. This project involves gently scraping and washing the exterior surfaces
on all four sides of the structure. Where mortar or brick failure is noticed, new mortar meeting historic
guidelines will be added. D. Trahan expressed the desire to appropriately address the repairs using SOI
standards.
Prior to painting, the rotted wood siding and trim on the existing bow windows (east elevations) will
be replaced, as will rotted fascia, soffits, and trim along all four upper reaches of the building. The box
gutter metal interiors were recently waterproofed, leaving the rotted exterior wooden sheaths to now be
replaced. They hope to ultimately find someone to rebuild these structures providing the cost isn’t
astronomical. On the west elevation, the plain, cracked, and peeling door will be replaced with a visually
appealing, weatherproof, paintable exterior door in the Arts and Craft style. The replacement will be a
composite as it lacks an overhang or portico and exposure to the elements would void any warrantee on a
fully wooden door.
One broken window will be replaced on the back (rear) elevation. The window is not salvageable.
Shims are currently holding a glass pane in place where the muntin has failed and the sill is rotted. This
window is not visible from any public thoroughfare; however, every attempt was made to replicate the
existing, single pane, six-over-six, while achieving better energy efficiency. A Marvin, all wood, double
glazed SDL was chosen as their grid system most closely resembles existing muntin widths. Marvin is also
the only company we found that would warranty exterior wooden windows. The building will be painted
in a 3-tone, early 20th century, Arts and Craft, earth tone palate by Sherman Williams. The colors were
chosen from their Historic Exteriors selection. These colors have been chosen to complement the roof color
and the recent repainting of a neighboring house with an earthy green Arts and Crafts palette.
To match chosen accent colors and the City street lighting, period appropriate black/wrought iron
elements will be added to the front elevation. These include replacing the rusty gold tone carriage lanterns
near the front door and adding wrought iron flower boxes on the second level. One box will be added to the
first level in the setback area. These boxes will not be duplicated on the entire lower level due to possible
use for trash by the public (a constant problem) and to leave room for climbing roses.
D. Trahan stated that she would like to swap out the proposed light fixture with a different style that
they feel is more period sensitive.  The Commissions were provided with the specification sheet for a
Maxim Carriage House lantern that would be installed near the front doorway.

The final step will be to grind down the stump in the front yard and replace this dirt area with raised
planting beds along the walls and a small old brick patio. Final material choices and a planting schedule
have not been determined, but we are leaning towards climbing roses and space for annuals.
The applicant also requested at the meeting to replace the second story John St facing windows which
have deteriorated and are noisy. The applicants were advised that because it was not listed as part of the
application, they would need to submit a new application to the Commissions focused on these windows.

The HLPC Commission was provided by staff with a drafted comment, in a redline format, that
pulled together the issues and comments raised at two workshop meetings held on February 9, 2023, and
March 9, 2023.  The comments had been circulated to all members in advance of the meeting, along with the
current standards for signage under the Pike Plan structure and a sketch that was prepared by the Commission
Architect Andrea Puetz.  Staff noted that in addition to information which was discussed at the workshops,
there was additional comment and information provided by Commissioners Puetz and McEvoy.
 M. Grunblatt questioned the terminology used in the paragraph on Maintenance on the last page.  He
indicated that the choice of the term hazard may not be appropriate, and the Commission settled on new
suggested wording for that sentence.
 Staff reminded the members that they also had requested to have the Pike Plan signage regulations added
into the Code, recognizing that at present, they are a free-standing document.  Staff asked if the HLPC wanted
any changes to those regulations as they exist, and none were proposed.
 Staff then recognized the sketch that Architect/Member Puetz had provided, noting that it was meant to
replace Figure 405.G.4.d Alignment….  It was also noted that the negative form shown in this figure and in the
one directly above should be removed and only show what is allowed to avoid confusion.
 No other comment was given.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed restoration of wooden features in-kind, restoration of brick and mortar in- kind, repainting the brick structure, replacing exterior light fixtures, creation of a patio area with raised planting bed in front yard, and installation of wrought iron flower boxes beneath second story windows at 89 John Street, in the Stockade Historic District, by the owners Raymond Lippert, MD. & Dara Trahan, if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-64, of the City of Kingston's Administrative Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: • that the proposed work is to take place at the 2.5 story 3 bay house situated on the north side of John St closer to the intersection of Green St, dating to the mid-19th-century. The Friends of Historic Kingston's Building-Structure Inventory Form dating from July 1987 records the following information: "It was probably built as income property by the family of one-time Ulster Co. Sheriff, John Kerr, who owned the corner of John & Green Streets. 89 John St was part of the same parcel of land until at least 1894. The first occupant of 89 John was-traced [to] George Gildersleeve who lived there from 1905 until 1920. He was treasurer of the Kingston Opera House and Mrs. E. Gildersleeve also operated a boarding house in the building during this period. By 1930, Joseph Mould, a clerk at the U&D RR, and I.M. Tapping, a nurse, lived in the house. From 1940 until after 1960, Asa Countryman, a city employee, and Mrs. R.E. Countryman, furnished rooms, were occupants of 89 John. In 1974, S. James Matthews, attorney, was listed occupant. In 1986, he and Ulster County Sanitation are listed at this address." • This work will cause a material change to the external appearance of the property and in doing so will aid in restoring and preserving the structure; • All woodwork, brick work, doors and rear window will be repaired in-kind; • The structure will be painted in a tritone scheme by Sherwin Williams: all brick will be Royucroft Copper Red (SW2839); soffits, gable trim, lintels, sills, and other wooden inserts beneath windows will be Renwick Beige (SW 2805); windows and rake will be Tricorn Black (SW 6258); • Iron window flower boxes will be installed on the second story, a brick patio with a raised flower bed will be constructed in the front, and light fixtures will be replaced with Maxim Carriage House 20" Traditional Bronze LED Outdoor Light Dimensions 20"H x 9"W x 13 extension from the wall; • Any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; • The Commission's approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding amended findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 6th day of April 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (MG-motion, NM-2nd, RT, KM, AP -yes)

The Commission Voted Unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application as presented and endorse the Preservation Notice of Action as adopted by the HLPC. (MD-motion, NM-2nd, BH, KM, JM -yes) RECOMMENDATION: 13. Form Based Code DISCUSSION on workshop meeting for the Historic Landmarks Preservation Commission to review and prepare comment back to the Common Council on the proposed City-wide Form Based Zoning Code. https://engagekingston.com/kingston-forward

The Commission voted unanimously to approve the drafted comment, noting that there will be no changes to the Pike Plan regulations on signs and they will be recognized, and incorporating the new sketch as submitted by A. Puetz, as follows: “City of Kingston Historic Landmarks Preservation Commission Recommended Comments on the Proposed Form Based Code April 6, 2023 General Note: The HLPC notes that the Common Council should also be looking at Chapter 264 of the City Code to recognize inconsistencies with new language as being presented in the FBC. Background: The Historic Landmarks Preservation Commission (HLPC) met in 2 workshop sessions to discuss the proposed Form-Based Code (FBC) for the City of Kingston. The dates for those sessions were February 9, 2023 and March 9, 2023. Each session was designed to cover specific sections of the FBC which are directly involving or related to the duties of the HLPC. The following bullets represent the findings and comments on the FBC as adopted: Article 4: Section 405.14 Architectural and Site Design Standards (Page 4.24) B. APPLICABILITY (Page 4.24) * 1. MODIFY 2nd sentence – The Architectural Standards, as identified in paragraphs E, G, H, I, J and K, of this Section, are encouraged (but not required) for Detached House, Carriage House, Duplex or Cottage Court Building Types. Design of structures should be compatible with the surrounding neighborhood, not necessarily discouraging other styles. E. BUILDING WALL MATERIALS & MASONRY DETAILING * 1. (f) – COMMENT - Understand this for some commercial structures, but this maybe shouldn't apply to all building types mentioned under B. above... both vinyl and aluminum are a mainstay type of material to use. Naturally there are other materials you could use in place of vinyl or aluminum clapboard, such as actual wood or maybe a hardiplank or other composite. Think it would be a mistake to prevent the everyday homeowner from being able to use those materials. Alternative materials can be expensive. Also, if you're in a situation where you're putting an addition on a house, would this prevent the use of trying to match materials? * 1. (g) QUESTION - There are outdoor malls and other shopfronts in the area that use EIFS. If any of them need repair or need to be modified, would this prevent that from happening? G. BUILDING DETAILS * 2. Roofs and Parapets (Page 4.29) - (g) This section references a sign panel allowed in a raised parapet section. There is no correlating standards on size, design etc., in the sign standard section. What regulates this? Materials? Illumination? Size? * 4. Columns (Page 4.30) - (b) All columns shall be spaced at regular intervals, to the greatest extent possible, and shall create openings…. - (c) The HLPC wants to recognize that there may be an appropriate occasion to make use of a “Faux” column which would not be a structural element of the building design. - (d) The HLPC members note that the alignment as shown in Figure 405.G.4.d, has the potential for the column capital to hold water, snow, ice, and debris, ultimately causing rot possibility. The HLPC questions if the figure is a “Blow-up” of Figure 405.14.G.4.c (above it), then without the roof detail, gives rise to more questions/interpretations. HLPC Provides Alternative Figure for consideration, which would require some minor notes for clarification. General Comment – Consideration should be given to removing the negative figure examples and just having the acceptable figures shown to avoid confusion. H. BUILDING HEIGHT (Page 4.31) * 1. COMMENT – The HLPC recognizes this as different from the present definition. The concern is that with the new wording the roof could potentially present a greater visual impact. * 3. Measuring STORIES: (a) A STORY is measured from finished floor level to the surface of the floor or eave of roof above…………. Article 4: Section 405.17 Signage Standards (Page 4.41) • ADD Signage Regulations that govern the installation of signs both under and along the “Pike Plan” structure on North Front and Wall Streets in the Stockade District. Regulations attached. E. PEDESTRIAN-ORIENTED SIGNS * 5. Pedestrian-Oriented Standards: - Page 4.43 – b. Projecting Signs (vii) This statement needs to be related to the following paragraph c. Marquee Signs, as it speaks to “A projecting marquee…..” Confusing and difficult to interpret. Is this meant to regulate the perpendicular element as shown in the photo with “c. Marquee Signs”? The dimensional height would not lend itself to thinking in that regard. Under “c. Marquee Signs” The HLPC questions if the intent is to regulate only the horizontal element as shown in the accompanying photograph? The width, height and quantity specifications would lend one to interpret it that way. Basically – Marquee signage needs to be re- worked for clarity and straight forward interpretation. - Page 4.44 – h. Sidewalk Signs – ADD (vii) Sidewalk Signs shall be appropriately secured and anchored in place in a manner suitable to the Department of Public Works. H. ICONIC SIGNS (Page 4.45) TYPO – ICONIC SIGNS such as barber poles, ….. shall be permitted as long as they comply with the otherwise applicable ….. Article 8: Section 405.26 L. Historic Landmarks Preservation Commission (Page 8.24) 2. Membership qualifications. (Page 8.24) * Change the current third sentence to read “All other members shall be residents…..” 6. Powers and duties. (Page 8.24) * To insert the following language as identified in red here in (a) (ii) “To review all applications for building permits, all outwardly physical installations and all appeals and applications transmitted to the Building Safety Officer which may affect any landmark or Landmark (L) District, and to make…..405.26.J.1.c. This provision shall exempt all in-kind restoration/rehabilitation work, painting using historic color collection palettes, minor modifications or alterations to the exterior, signage when in compliance with the regulations herein, as determined by the Planning Administrator to be suitable for a determination of impact issued on an administrative level. 7. Landmark or Landmark District designation procedure. (Page 8.25) * (f) The HLPC questioned the method of ratification by the Common Council needed. Recommend changing the second sentence to remove certain language as follows: “The designation shall be effective upon ratification through ordinance by the Common Council. 8. Landmarks and Landmark(L) Districts. (Page 8.26) * (a) (ii) The Stockade Area of Kingston, New York, consisting of eight blocks bounded by Clinton Avenue, Main Street, Green Street and North Front Street, together with protective perimeter, is the site of the stockade ordered built by Peter Stuyvesant in 1658 and successive extensions under English rule. In this area there were two conflicts with Esopus Lenni Lenape people Indian massacres, one in 1659-60 and one in 1663-64, as well as the location of the founding of the first government of the State of New York in 1777 and burned by the British that same year. This area contains architecture dating back to the 17th and 18th Century including the corner of Crown and John Streets with four pre-Revolutionary stone houses, one on each corner of the intersection. In addition to the distinctive pre- Revolutionary stone houses, the district has 19th Century structures in Federal Period, Greek Revival, Italianate and Second Empire and Queen Anne styles as well as the mid-19th Century stone Old Dutch Church, a National Landmark. * (a) (ii) (2) TYPO – This area contains architecture ……. And cultural organizations of the past. * (a) (iii) The Rondout Landmark District consisting of the area as shown on the Regulating Map and described as: The Rondout Historic District encompasses the area sloping down to and featuring the waterfront on Rondout Creek. Rondout was rapidly transformed from farmland into a thriving maritime village after the opening in 1828 of the Delaware and Hudson Canal with its terminus here. Plentiful jobs on the canal, in boatyards and shipping, in industries such as brick and cement manufacturing as well as bluestone, drew a melting pot of immigrants whose imprint is still visible in the rich legacy of commercial buildings, cast-iron storefronts, homes and churches in the district despite losses due to urban renewal in the 1960’s. * (a) (iv) The Fair Street Landmark District consisting of the area as shown on the Regulating Map and described as: Starting in the mid-19th Century, a long line of distinguished residences representing several architectural styles were erected along Fair Street extending out from the Stockade District as affluent people began moving out from the Stockade District and building substantial structures. The tree-shaded street has significant examples of the Italianate, Second Empire, Queen Anne, and Colonial Revival architecture. * (a) (v) The Chestnut Street Historic District consisting of the area shown on the Regulating Map and described as: The district encompasses both West and East Chestnut Streets offering splendid examples of various architectural styles including Italianate, French Second Empire, Queen Anne, Colonial Revival, and Italian Renaissance many set on expansive lawns. In the 19th Century, on West Chestnut Street at the top of the hill above Rondout, several of the most affluent and powerful business people in Rondout built large homes, some with magnificent views of the Hudson River and Catskill Mountains. * (b) (ii) (4) Maintenance. “Preventive maintenance is required in order to assure that these buildings, spaces, elements and details are preserved. Failure to provide this Deliberate neglect and/or lack of preventive maintenance that presents an issue of public safety or rapid deterioration of a structure shall be a violation of this article. 9. Review Procedure. * ADD (e) It shall be the further duty of the Commission to exercise judgement in accord with the guidance of the US Secretary of the Interior Standards for Rehabilitation. “ HLPC VOTE: NM- Motion, RT – second, MG, KM, AP – yes Next Joint Meeting: May 4th, 2023 This meeting will be live-streamed at the City of Kingston YouTube channel: https://www.youtube.com/c/CityofKingstonNY

items.title: Adoption of the Minutes of April 6th, 2023, Meeting. a. HAC Adoption of the Minutes of April 6th, 2023, Meeting.:
#106-122 Green Street. Replacement of all windows
items.discussion:
Selina S. Guendel, Regent, and Kaaren Davis, Treasurer of the of the Wiltwyck Chapter of the
NSDAR, and their window contractor, Harley Davis , presented to the HLPC and the HAC .   S. Guendel began
by identifying the new information which had been submitted with this new application.  Part of the information
included two evaluations and resume background for different parties.  She noted that the s taff had already
reviewed the qualifications of S. Crew and identified that he was not qualified earlier on, but they still submitted
his information.  E. Dickerman did note that he had conferred with E. Majors (a known preservation expert and
identified as someone whom Mr. Crews worked with) and was told that he is more of a painter, not a
preservation expert.
Staff noted that a partial conditions assessment report had been completed in -house, but that because staff did
not have the ability to get close, the report was not complete.  That document detailed the type of information
which staff believed was necessary for the Commissions to make a determination on work.  It had been
distributed to both members and the applicants and staff asked if the DAR representatives had looked at it and
what thoughts they had.  They admittedly had not reviewed.
Commissioner McEvoy read excerpts from a communication received by the City from SHPO (Dated May 26,
2022), and that it identified the key elements of an assessment.  S. Guendel stated that she was not familiar with
the letter.  K. Davis  noted that they misunderstood the previous requests of the Commissioners to mean they
wanted documentation of the proposed windows, which is why only the specifications for the proposed
windows had been provided.  She also noted that they had read literature which stated reasoning to believe this
was in-kind replacement and therefore, no review was required.  K. McEvoy again referenced language from the
SHPO letter that it “Proposed replacement of historic windows is never considered a replace in-kind project even
if it is wood with wood.”
Commissioners inquired why the applicants did not seek out professional  preservationists/craft persons that
specialize in this type of work.  Staff noted they had provided names and contact information.  The applicants
stated that they did make some calls but did not get returns.
The applicants stated that they do not believe the existing windows are restorable or have historic significance
as they believe they were replaced in the 1920s. Staff asked if they had documentation from when the w indows
were replaced. The applicants said they will look.
H. Davis had brought a sample window of the proposed replacements for 106-122 Green Street.  Although it was
sealed in clear wrapping,  he discussed the attributes and at the end of the overall discussion, Commission
members had an opportunity to look at it up closely .  In discussion, Mr. Davis noted that all  the structure’s
windows are slated to be replaced.  He did, however, state that 6 of the windows could be restored.  He noted
that they are not all on the same building face.

Commissioners stated they do not have enough information to make an informed determination because the
applicants have not adequately documented photographical ly and textually the conditions of the existing
wooden windows.
It was determined that a site visit might best allow staff and a couple of representatives of each Commission to
better determine the conditions and allow for documentation.  The applicants ag reed to coordinate that with
staff soon, so that there would be time to provide information before the next meeting.  Commissioners Puetz,
Tonner and Howland expressed interest.

decisions.text: The Commission voted to table the application and to schedule a time for commissioners from the HLPC and the HAC, along with the applicants, their contractor, the Planning Director, and the Historic Preservation Administrator to visit the site for a close inspection of the window’s existing conditions. (AP- motion, RT-2nd, KM, NM - yes).
The Commission tabled the item and endorsed a site inspection as determined by the HLPC. (MD-motion, NM-2nd, JM, KM, BH - yes) HAC APPLICATIONS:

items.title: #16-18 Gill St. Painting exterior, porch removal & replacement, window replacement, side room addition
items.discussion:
Karolina Hart, applicant/owner was present to discuss  the work already completed and what
remains to be undertaken.  The Building Department stopped them as work was occurring and directed them to
HAC for review.

They have removed and replaced the pre-existing wooden porches and railing systems along the street frontage
with black standing seam steel awnings.  The railings will also be steel and have yet to be installed.  The stoops
and steps remain as original. K. Hart noted that she is working with J. Stinemire, PE, on the structural
components.
They have also added a mudroom on the structure’s south side which is visible from Gill Street. An older, similar
addition to the structure is visible from the northside too. Both additions  will be clad in black standing seam
metal siding.
All windows in the structure ha ve been replaced with white double hung windows with modern triple pane
replacements. The new windows are Drutex SA PVC windows, IGLO 5 Classic treated black.
Lastly, the applicant seeks to repaint the brick structure, already painted red, with Benjamin Moore Walker
Green #CW -510. The front doors will be painted Benjamin Moore Sun Porch yellow #2023 -30, and the
structure’s trim and exterior metalwork will be Benjamin Moore Black #HC-190.  Color samples were shown.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application as presented. (MD-motion, JM-2nd, BH, KM, NM - yes)

items.title: #206 W Chestnut St. Replacing roof on garage/shed, in-kind woodwork, painting, garage door replacement
items.discussion:
Sjoerd Dijk, the applicant, presented to the HAC their plans to  replace the Montrepose Ave -
facing garage’s existing three-tab brown asphalt shingle roof with ABC Hunter Green Lokseam standing steel
roof. The applicant will remove the existing roof and install the proposed steel roof themselves.

In addition, to the proposed roof replacement the owner intends to paint the soffits, doors, and trim Hunter
Green to match the roof.

Staff noted that the application also seeks approval for additional work to the structure to be carried out in the
future. This work would include hiring a company to replace the left two rolling wood doors with metal doors
with flat black trim. These doors will have full/floor to ceiling glass paneling.   The existing garage door to the
right would get replaced with a fixed glass panel wall with black trim, and an entry door painted Hunter Green
to match the roof.  Staff asked if the use would continue as a garage or if there was another occupancy planned.
S. Dijk stated it would stay as garage use.  It was noted that information to determine authorization for the door
replacements is incomplete and should be separated out until documentation is provided.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application for the roof replacement and painting the existing garage doors with a hunter green to match the new roof. items.title: #28 Hudson St. Installation of 7 PV (2.590kW) roof mount panels
items.discussion:
Patricia Colella, representing Sunrun was present to represent the owner.  The application is  to
install seven Prexos Series 6 solar panels on the rear (east) roof of the dwelling with an 18-degree pitch, that will
only be visible from Spring Street. The panels will be mounted to the roof using Snaprack  railing systems, in
combination with Type I, or Type II fire rated modules.

Mighty Engineering Co. has submitted a structural evaluation of the roof in anticipation of the installation and
confirms its load carrying capacity meets the requirements for installation. The sub panel, Sunrun Meter, and
inverters will be mounted at the northeast corner visible from Spring Street.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application as presented. (MD-motion, JM-2nd, KM, NM, BH - yes)

items.title: #10 Dietz Court. Expansion of garage and living space by 1610sq/ft, including front porch addition and steps, window replacement and alterations, installation of 27 solar panels to roof, rear deck addition

items.discussion:
Andrew and Sonia Wright , Architects were present to represent the property owner.  They
explained that the owner is undertaking a significant amount of work on both the exterior and interior of the
structure, including  modifications to the existing front façade, constructing a side  and rear addition , a new
second floor addition, along with site work which includes landscaping, stonework and solar panels at 10 Dietz
Court.

S. Wright reviewed the work elements as outlined in the application paperwork, most notable is the street face
appearance that will be altered with a new front porch, new materials and facings and a substantial landscaping
overhaul. The original form of the structure will change with the addition, however its placement to the side and
rear will be offset and the character of the structure will continue to be compatible with the neighboring homes.
Originally, the solar panels were going to be located on ground level and they have subsequently placed them on
the roof to minimize the impact on the property.

Staff noted that the applicants had submitted a photograph, taken from a vantage point in the Rondout Historic
District (on West Pierpont, between Wurts  and Adams) to show that the back side of the structure does have
minimal visibility from that historic area.  That was one reason to move the panels to the roof, so that additional
clearing of property would not create a more substantive impact visually.

S. Wright reviewed the intended finishes which are planned to be used around the exterior of the structure.  They
are seeking to use natural materials and more locally sources products.  Every effort is being made to match
closely the existing exterior brick, in color and size.

In general , the home will be renovated to provide a more open floor design, and one that embodies energy
conservation measures.

Commissioner Howland stated that she was in favor of the overall scope of work.  Commissioner Del  Priore
echoed the opinion and thought that the renovations were appropriately scaled and compatible with the
neighborhood.

H. Maish, owner was present.  He explained that he wishes  to repaint the full exterior of their

wooden clapboard dwelling, presently painted a creamy tan with white trim. The proposed paint scheme will be
Benjamin Moore Nimbus Gray (2131 -50) and the trim will remain white. The street facing wooden porch’s
flooring and stairs will be repainted Benjamin Moore Stone (2112 -40).  Sample colors were shared with Board
members to consider.

Tyson McCasland, Timely Signs, was present to represent the applicant.  The proposal is to
install two double sided white letters on blue background hanging signs produced by Timely Signs for the
Kingston Bottle Shop, LLC, DBA Kingston Wine Company:
• 37.625” w x 10.125” h - 3/4"thick Extira; V-Carved elements, primed and painted to match called out PMS

Colors. Lower (Bottle) Panel
• 48 ‘w x 10.125" h – 3/4"thick Extira; V -Carved elements, primed and painted to match called out PMS
Colors.

Both signs will be hung together as a single unit, from the existing hanging bracket on the structure but will use
new eyehooks and side straps.

The Commissions both noted the shape, using a bottle in the design was attractive and provides the unique touch
that is appropriate for the Rondout.

Staff noted that the overall dimensions of the 2 signs together do not exceed the maximum square footage, and
because they work in tandem, that they were looked at as a single unit.  The ZEO will need to review and concur
that position.

T. McCasland also noted that they recognize the need to have insurance carried naming the City and would
provide.

Tyson McCasland, Timely Signs, was present to represent the applicant.  The proposal is to
install two signs from the Pike Plan for Jennifer Lynn Interiors, an interior design company:

1x- single sided 39” w x 14.75” x .75” thick painted PVC panel with white vinyl applied, hung on existing hooks.
This is the sign that will be hung parallel to the street.

1x- double sided 60” w x 14”h x .75” thick painted PVC with white vinyl applied, hung on existing hooks. This is
the sign that will be hung beneath the canopy, perpendicular to the street.

T. McCasland stated that both signs will be painted Benjamin Moore Hale Navy (HC-154) with Plotter Cut Hp
White Vinyl Logo. All hardware will be painted black.   Each sign will have a clearance to grade of 106” or 8.8’,
meeting the required criteria.

It was noted that insurance naming the City of Kingston as additionally insured will be required.

Carol Amper, owner, was present.  She reviewed the plans to  repaint the exterior of the
structure from its present pink and white scheme to a quad scheme based on a palette of Benjamin Moore’s
Historic colors:
• Rockport Gray HC-105: Proposed base or body color. See below image for mockup.
• Great Barrington Green HC-122: Proposed accent color.
• Somerville Red HC-62: Proposed accent color.
• New London Burgundy HC-61: proposed accent color.

The Commission’s reviewed the renderings that showed the colors and the placement.  She produced actual color
samples, noting that the ones which were with the submission lost the ir true color when reproduced and she
wanted to make sure that the choices were clearly demonstrated.

Prior to repainting the structure, the applicant intends to scrape off old flaking paint from wooden features,
repair woodwork, repair or replace rested and rooted metal, flashing as needed, clean bricks, and caulk and fill
in gaps as needed. Images of the structure’s current conditions are included below. Paint should not be removed
with any blasting type activity, as there is potential for damage of the underlying materials.

Staff noted that the painting work is being proposed as part of work that is funded through a municipal grant.
The application also speaks of replacement of windows on the building’s  front façade.  Staff noted that as with
other window replacement projects, the Commission should require the applicant to submit clear
documentation, from qualified individuals to demonstrate the existing conditions and to provide for a
determination of whether a restoration may be appropriate.  Also, more information on what is being considered

as replacement units is necessary.  The Commissions agreed to separate out the windows from the painting and
only consider the one at this time, noting more documentation to be provided on the windows.

Tyson McCasland, Timely Signs was present to represent the owner.  He noted that although
the application had 3 signs, they are modifying the signage, by reducing it to 2 signs, but with each measuring 5’
x 5’.  These will be temporary signs  on the Fair Street side of the Sena te Garage Building produced by Timely
Signs, and which will be mounted between the central windows on the ground floor. Each sign will have a black
background with white and orange text detailing Cowork Kingston’s working space; one sign will have imagery.

Staff recognized that the applicant has been advised that variances are needed for the temporary signage, for both
the number and for the duration.  T. McCasland questioned if the variances were to be granted and they
periodically, every few months, changed the sign message, would the variance cover that aspect.  Staff did not
believe so, but they were directed to confirm with the ZEO.

The applicant, Tom Kreuger, presented to the Commission images and a written description of
the site’s current conditions along with his plans for restoring 35 Wurts St which includes in -kind restoration
of the wooden soffits, fascia, box gutters, and the restoratio n of the slate roof. Additional materials which had
been submitted earlier in the day were provided to the Commission members by staff, noting that these are future
work elements, and that they will need more detail provided, but the idea was to provide a comprehensive
understanding of the owner’s commitment to full restoration. The applicant plans to undertake the additional
work to restore the structure in Phases and will return to the Commissions for approval as needed.
The Commissions discussed the uniqueness of the slate roof and its connection to the adjoining church building.
Staff noted that they have been working to assist the owner in locating a contractor who might be able to do a
restoration project on the roof, versus the replacement. T. Krueger spoke about the submitted synthetic slate
material specifications and the advantages of using this material, citing durability and cost. M. DelPriore stated
that he liked the use of the synthetic product as an option. A. Puetz stated that she would forwar d a name for
slate work.
The Commission’s focused on scaling back the original submission to remove the slate roof work from the repair
and restoration work of the soffits, fascia,  and box gutters. T. Krueger mentioned that he would like to offer a
possible alternative on the gutter and have them slightly modified to have an exterior component, but not alter
the overall appearance. It was agreed that staff could review a modification and if finding it not to be a visual
impediment, could authorize the change.

J. Fish, Architect; and A. Monk, owner , were present.   Jim Fish presented the  design for a
dwelling on a lot adjacent to the applicant’s home which is intended to be occupied by a family member in the
immediate future.

He discussed the positioning and size of the structure, noting that it will be located close to the roadway due to
slope of land.  He presented Board’s of the drawings to show the different elevations and floor plan.  The
Commissions questioned the owner and architect as to why the street facing side is a bare wall which is not
consistent with the rest of the neighborhood’s streetscape. A. Monk informed the Commissions that it is planned
for some low shrubbery to be planted which will help to soften the appearance.  J. Fish noted that, visually, the
structure is not seen when travelling in either direction along the st reet until you are almost immediately at the
property and that is why they tried to focus the design on a direction that would benefit the user.  S. Cahill noted
that the city is presently undertaking a project which will adopt new form -based code zoning and that this
project would not be acceptable in that context.   S. Cahill also noted that the owner’s  own structure has street
frontage and that the Commissions should look at how this contributes to the streetscape as a whole, and
whether it is compatible.  Most Commission members of both the HLPC and the HAC agreed that the face along
the street should be modified in some manner.  The suggestion of having  a faux garage door design added  was
brought up and would be one possibility.

S. Cahill advised that as presented, a variance for a side yard setback would be required.  Other variances may be
necessary, and the architect or owner should contact the City ZEO to review the plans also.

Staff informed the Commissions that the Planning Board will review this project on May 15th and recommended

that the HLPC and HAC table the item for review by the Planning Board , to allow for consideration and
development of alternatives for the street face elevation, and for a zoning review.
