items.title: Adoption of the Minutes of May 4th, 2023, Meeting. a. HAC Adoption of the Minutes of May 4th, 2023, Meeting:
#71 Abruyn St: Replace front wooden steps and railing system with bluestone and metal
items.discussion:
The applicant, Andrea Watson-Smith, was absent but staff presented an overview of the project
to the Commissioners. The applicant seeks to replace the existing front steps that are made of wood with
bluestone steps, retaining the wooden railing that exists.  The applicant submitted photographs of the exist ing
conditions and a photograph of what the new entryway stairs will look like. Staff researched the structure’s
history and determined that the structure never had bluestone stairs and that the front porch was altered two or
three times since its construction. The applicant intends to hire Vargas Outdoor Comfort as the contractor to do
the work.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application for the front entryway stairs replacement with bluestone and the retention of the wooden railings. (JM-motion, KM-2nd, BH, NM-yes).

items.title: #7 Burnett St: Roof replacement, chimney removal and solar panel installation with superstructure
items.discussion:
The applicant, Richard Baronio, presented to the Commission his plans to do the following:
• to replace the existing asphalt roof in-kind;
• strengthen the existing rafters;
• remove the structure’s gable-end ridge chimneys;
• replace the box gutters with aluminum gutters;
• install a steel superstructure atop the workshop for the installation of solar panels;
• install solar panels on the southwestern facing roof of the dwelling.

Staff and Commissioners explained that this structure was recently surveyed by city consultants. This structure
is identified as part of a potential historic district and has potential for individual nomination. Therefore, removal
of the chimneys and box gutters will weaken the structure’s historical integrity and adversely affect the Wilbur
neighborhood’s streetscape.
R. Baronio noted that chimneys are not functioning for any purpose, and he wishes to decommission them.  He
expressed serious concerns over the Staff and Commissioner’s desire to see the chimneys and box gutters retained
and cited his inability to fund such work but did note that he is awaiting a sale of property in the city to go
through for funds to use on the current project.  The applicant claimed to have not known their home was within
the Heritage Area  when he purchased the property.  He was also not aware that there was a project for a
neighborhood survey, and that his property might be eligible for State and National Register status.  Staff stated
that they would forward the excerpts of the draft document to the property owner and seek possible funding to
assist.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application for the in-kind roof replacement, strengthening of the dwelling’s rafters, installation of the solar panel systems as presented and noted that the chimneys and box gutters would be restored and not removed . (JM- motion, NM-2nd, BH, KM- yes).

items.title: #582 Broadway: Restoration of vitrolite store front façade and awning
items.discussion:
Innis Lawrence of Kingston 582 Broadway, LLC, presented to the Commissioners their plans to
restore 582 Broadway’s Street facing façade in -kind. Historically, the façade was clad in black vitrolite panels
beneath and surrounding the fenestration and doorways. At some point, the black vitrolite panels were changed
to white which is the color the applicant intends to retain. All broken and missing panels will be replaced with
spare pieces that were in the basement when they took ownership.   The applicant intends to install a fixed metal
awning produced by NYC Signs & Awnings, that will be stripped to match the original awning and will display
the business’s name on its street-facing end. The awning will sit at 10feet above the sidewalk, well above the 84”
code requirement. Abo ve the awning the corrugated steel paneling (formerly vitrolite panels) will be painted
white to match the vitrolite panels near the ground.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application for the in-kind restoration of the white vitrolite paneled storefront, and to allow Staff to work with the applicant on the final approval for the awning. Insurance naming the City of Kingston as additionally insured will be provided prior to the awni ng installation and meeting Section 358 -9 of the Code. (NM-motion, KM-2nd, BH, JM- yes).

items.title: #693-701 Broadway: Install prefabricated, public toilet facility
items.discussion:
Radio Kingston Corporation, presented to the Commission their plans to include in their  site
redevelopment a “Portland Loo” © (public toilet). The Portland Loo is a solar -powered free standing toilet
structure that self-cleans and can accommodate up to 300 flushes per day. Radio Kingston intends to install and
maintain this public toilet to assist their neighborhood where it is badly needed. It will have a direct connection
to municipal sewers and use city water. Those connections will need to be verified by the KWD and the Plumbing
Inspector. It will be located off Liberty Street side of the property and the applicant should be directed to contact
the city Zoning Officer to confirm any setbacks. It would be an accessory structure and visible from both
Broadway and Liberty. All maintenance of the unit will be by the property owner, and it is i ntended to be open
to the public. The structure will be painted green to blend into the landscaped area it is situated within and will
be open from dawn to dusk.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application for the installation of a green Portland Loo on the Liberty Street side of the Radio Kingston Corporation’s property which will become a privately man aged greenspace, with the condition that the applicant secure a zoning sign-off. (NM-motion, JM-2nd, BH, KM - yes). HAC/HLPC JOINT REGULAR BUSINESS:

items.title: #106-122 Green Street. Replacement of all windows
items.discussion:
Selina S. Guendel, Regent, and Kaaren Davis, Treasurer of the of the Wiltwyck Chapter of the
NSDAR, contacted staff via email, on May 26th, 2023, requesting that a decision on their project be tabled until
the July 6th, 2023, meeting, recognizing that a agreed site visit was not able to take place yet.  The additional time
will allow for the applicant to work with staff and others to schedule a site visit. Commissioners Puetz, Tonner
and Howland continued to express interest.

decisions.text: The Commission voted to table the application and to schedule a time for commissioners from the HLPC and the HAC, along with the applicants, their contractor, the Planning Director, and the Historic Preservation Administrator to visit the site for a close inspection of the window’s existing conditions. ( AP- motion, RT-2nd, KM, NM – yes; MG recusal).
The Commission tabled the item and endorsed a site inspection as determined by the HLPC. (NM-motion, KM-2nd, BH, JM- yes)

items.title: #126-128 Hudson St. Two-bedroom residential unit in owner’s yard
items.discussion:
J. Fish, Architect; and A. Monk, owner, returned to the Commissions for review of their alteration
to include a faux carriage door on the Hudson Street facing side of their design for a dwelling on a lot adjacent to
the applicant’s home which is intended to be occupied by a family member in the immediate future.

Commissioners for both the HLPC and the HAC agreed that the face along the street was significantly improved
with the addition of this design element, because prior to its inclusion, travelers would be presented with a large
blank wall. The applicant confirmed the installation of the carriage style streetlights will be installed adjacent to
the faux door and the board and batten siding across the structure’s entire façade will continue.  Because a “faux”
door is being added, landscaping p reviously discussed will no longer be installed, instead there will be small
planters to either side to provide more definition.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed two-bedroom residential unit in owner's yard at 126-128 Hudson Street in the Rondout neighborhood by Andrew Monk, if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405 -64, of the City of Kings ton's Administrative Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: - that the proposed work is to take place on a vacant lot, identified as 126-128 Hudson Street, adjacent to the owner's personal dwelling at 138 Hudson Street, and for which no historical information could be sourced beyond its known proximity to the Rondout Creek which historically served as a industrial center and transportation corridor for the City of Kingston; - that the proposed structure will be a 1,273 SF, single family dwelling, with two bedrooms, that will not directly face Hudson Street; -that the applicant has returned to the Commission with hardiboard for siding material and earth tone color, windows, doors, solar panel and associated equipment and incorporation of street facing doorway to resemble Carriage House style and design; -that the project, being within the Rondout area, must notify the Planning Department in the event that potentially sensitive archaeological/cultural materials are unearthed during excavation practices; -that the project has obtained site plan approval by the Planning Board, and the Commission notes that documentation addressing storm water and utility connections will be addressed as well as the geophysical stability of the proposed site through Building Department review; - any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; - the Commission's approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding amended f indings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 1st day of June, 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (MG-motion, RT-2nd, AP, KM, NM – yes).

The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application for the construction of a new single unit dwelling at 126-128 Hudson Street according to the plans presented. (NM-motion, KM-2nd, BH, JM- yes).

items.title: #35 Wurts St. Restoration/replacement of slate roof, restoring the soffits and related woodwork
items.discussion:
The applicant, Tom Kreuger, presented to images and a written description of the site’s current
conditions along with his plans for restoring 35 Wurts St which includes in -kind restoration of the wooden
soffits, fascia, box gutters, and the restoration of the slate roof. The applicant plans to undertake additional work
to restore the structure in Phases and will return to the Commissions for approval as needed.

T. Kreuger stated that he has decided to move forward and restore the slate roof (pending the cost estimates are
not prohibitive and not feasible);  restore in-kind the existing wooden windows , replacing those missing at the
ground level beneath the front porch with new wooden windows. Window work will be completed by Emily
Major of White Clay Kill Preservation, LLC.

The applicant presented to the Commissions his need to treat exposed wood near the soffits, fascia, and box
gutters with stain. Staff requested the ability to work with the applicant at the desk level to determine an
appropriate neutral pallet, such as mahogany, for stain.

T. Kreuger also discussed the severely deteriorated chimney on the rear of the house.  Photos of the chimney were
viewed indicating the low visibility of the unit from Wurts Street. Commission members acknowledged that the
cost of repairing this chimney may hinder the applicant’s ability to replace the slate roof.  They weighed the
benefit of retaining and restoring a decommissioned chimney to having the slate roof repaired and determined
the investment would be better placed in the roof.

There was discussion over the base masonry and the stucco covering the stone.  Commission members agreed to
allow for the removal of the topcoat, exposing the stone foundation and provide for the restoration of such.

For the off -street parking, T. Kreuger stated that he would be reactivating the curb cut and would also be
uncovering/restoring/or if needed replacing the bluestone tracks only to provide for an area for vehicles to pull
off street.

Along the side of the structure wh ere the new driveway will be restored, T. Kreuger noted that he intends to
install a gas meter for the structure service.  It would be located to the back and will have screening.  It was
discussed that staff would be able to work directly with the applica nt on the screening type and placement.
Placement of an HVAC unit will also be considered in close proximity, and this will require further review once
size, location, and supporting elements are better placed.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed restoration of the soffits, fascia, wooden box gutters, and slate roof at 35 Wurts Street in the Rondout Historic District by Thomas Kreuger, if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405 -64, of the City of Kings ton's Administrative Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: • that the proposed work is to take place at the two-story brick Second Empire dwelling dating between 1858 and 1870 that stands adjacent to the Trinity Methodist Church at the corner of Wurts and Hunter St which the October 21st, 1971, Building-Structure In ventory Form prepared by the Friends of Historic Kingston states "was the parsonage for the neighboring Methodist church. The residence retains its original decorative features and has received no major modern alterations. It is one of the most intact and important structures of its type and style in the district"; • that the applicant will replace in -kind the slate roof that displays a decorative floral design that matches a similar design on the neighboring church; • that the applicant may remove the rear chi mney without adversely impacting the structure's integrity because of its severe degradation; • that the applicant shall restore and rebuild all wooden sash windows in accordance with NPS Preservation standards and install wood sash windows where units are missing; • that the applicant shall re -point masonry as needed and shall follow the guidelines stipulated in NPS Pres. Briefs 1 & 2, exposing the stone foundation and not replacing with stucco; • that the applicant shall return to the Commission for review for subsequent phases of their restoration of 35 Wurts Street or any changes to plans discussed at this meeting; • that the applicant shall restore the 2 -track bluestone driveway, using the existing curb cut, uncovering or replacing the bluestone; • that the applicant shall install a gas meter on the north side of the structure (along the driveway) close to the structure's rear which shall be screened by either a fence of shrubbery as approved by staff; • that the applicant shall install a HVAC unit near the gas mete r and shielded by the same screen and which will be subject to further review upon submission of the unit's dimensions, make, model, and the manner with which it's lines shall be run into the dwelling; • that the applicant shall work with staff on replacing and restoring new balustrade on the front porch to replicate original details; • any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; • the Commission's approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding amended fi ndings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 1st day of June 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (AP-motion, RT-2nd; NM, KM, MG- yes)

The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application as presented and endorse the Preservation Notice of Action as adopted by the HLPC. (JM-motion, NM-2nd; BH, KM- yes)

items.title: #24-26 Hunter St. & 33-35 West Union St: Construct off street parking lot for use by owner
items.discussion:
Joseph Minuta and Japheth Aleyakpo, on behalf of Union Church, LLC, presented to the
commission their client’s intention to redevelop the existing parking lot at the site to initially accommodate  14
off street parking spaces, green space, and a walkway that will allow residents at Unions Church Hill’s
properties across the street easy access to Cornell Park. Both internal and external sidewalks, along the curb
cuts, will be made of dyed concrete that mimics blue stone and will conform with the ADA 5-foot-wide
requirements. The Commissions discussed with the applicants a newer design that was recently discussed
with staff to reduce the parking to 12 spaces, continuing the tandem parking design, but allowing for smaller
curb cuts on either side, but also providing a central green area which might accommodate additional trees.

Curb cuts will be present on both the Hunter and Union Street sides. Several trees, shrubbery, and grass will
be planted to further landscape the proposed green space.
HLPC DISCISION: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to
find as fact that the proposed construction of a parking lot and green space at 24-26 Hunter St. & 33-35 West
Union St in the Rondout Historic District by Union Church Hill, LLC, if done according to the plans reviewed
at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-64, of the City of Kingston's
Administrative Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons:
• that the proposed work is to take place on two presently vacant lots one of which was previously owned by
the Seventh Day Adventist Church of West Unions St and which according to a July 14th, 1975, Building-
Structure Inventory Form produced by the Friends of Historic Kingston was once the site of a barn that
appeared on the circa 1880 Burleigh map of Kingston. At the time the form was written, this was one of the
last surviving barns in the district with an original carriage door";
• that the applicant shall continue to use the two lots as for parking for the adjacent 24 West Union, 25-27
Abeel St, and 38-40 West Union St residential units under development by the same applicant;
• that the applicant shall landscape the green spaces with trees;
• that the applicant shall accommodate the 5-foot sidewalk requirements for the district;
• that the applicant shall incorporate a curb cut that includes the width of the lots;
• Any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted
application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out;
• The Commission's approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's
Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies;
Based on the preceding amended findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 1st day of June 2023, the
Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described
herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the
foregoing motion. (MG motion, RT-2nd, AP, NM, KM-yes)

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application as presented and endorse the Preservation Notice of Action as adopted by the HLPC. (JM motion, NM-2nd; BH, KM - yes)

items.title: #25-27 Abeel St: Construct a 3-family residential building and supporting infrastructure
items.discussion:
Joseph Minuta and Japheth Aleyakpo, on behalf of Union Church, LLC, presented the plan to
construct a three-unit residential rental property at 25-27 Abeel Street and on their adjacent lot, 38-40 West
Union Street. The new buildings will be joined with a party wall, but the elevations of each will be off set.  Staff
noted that when the original design was submitted the design was very different and the applicants have re-
submitted a design that makes a firmer step toward compatibility with the Rondout District, bringing in

materials, and fenestration but also incorporating some modern style features to set it apart from the historic
structures.  Each building will be two stories in height, with design elements drawn from other 19th-century
brick storefronts throughout the Rondout neighborhood. Windows will have clearly defined sills and lintels.
Window materials will likely be made of metal treated black to match other black metal features, such as
railings, awnings, and doors that evoke a post-industrial theme. The applicants reviewed all of the materials
with the Commissions and also discussed finishes.
On the Abeel Street side, the structures will have cantilevered decks that wrap around to sidewalk/walkways
on ground level. A new staircase will be constructed that will provide a access walk to the street.  The
Commissions reviewed the existing photos and some plans to see how the existing retaining wall along the
roadway and the bedrock will be cleared off and exposed.  Remnants of an older staircase are being sought to
try and restore if possible.
The roof top will have green spaces, one per unit, separated by fencing, but that can be linked via gates.
Along West Union Street, there will be 5 parking spaces with electric vehicle charging stations available to
residents. Additionally, parking will be across the street at 24-26 Hunter & 33-35 West Union Street.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action as Unlisted under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed construction of a three unit residential structure at 25-27 Abeel Street in the Rondout Historic District by Union Church Hill, LLC, if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-64, of the City of Kingston's Administrative Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: • that the proposed work is to take place at the second vacant lot to the south of the circa 1864 Seventh Day Adventist Church on a lot that is bordered by Abeel Street to the east and West Union to the west and which is located mid-way between Post and Wurts Streets; • that the proposed structure shall be a three units’ residential structure and with a street facing facade composed of brick and steel which matches the existing character of the neighborhood and the Rondout District's existing storefront designs; • that the structure's windows shall be 1/1 black steel with clearly demarcated sills and lintels that correspond with the district's fenestration; • that the structure shall have corbelled cornices, corner-based trim work that shall frame the structure's bays, and that the overall design shall favor bi-lateral symmetry; • Any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; • The Commission's approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding amended findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 1st day of June 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (MG motion, RT-2nd, AP, KM, NM-yes)

The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application as presented and endorse the Preservation Notice of Action as adopted by the HLPC. (JM motion, KM-2nd; BH, NM - yes)

items.title: #38-40 West Union St. Construct a 3-family residential building and supporting infrastructure

items.title: #24 West Union St: Convert an existing building to a 3-family residence
items.discussion:
Joseph Minuta and Japheth Aleyakpo, on behalf of Union Church, LLC, presented the plan to
restore the façade and adaptively reuse the interior of the former Seventh Day Adventist Church at 24 West
Union Street, by creating two or three residential units. Staff questioned whether the existing windows will be
altered or replaced. J. Minuta clarified that the structure’s existing fenestration will be retained, and all existing
windows are to be restored according to NPS Standards. The drawings will be corrected to show no changes to
the façade.  A late dated red brick addition to the structures southwest with no historical value will be
removed.
The owner’s intention is to undertake the work so that the property will be eligible for both the State and
National Registers and ultimately they will be able to access the preservation tax credits.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed adaptive reuse of the Kingston Seventh Day Adventist Church into a two or three unit residential dwelling at 24 West Union Street in the Rondout Historic District by Union Church Hill, LLC, if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-64, of the City of Kingston's Administrative Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: • that the proposed work is to take place at the circa 1864 church, remodeled in 1940 to its current form and which a July 13th, 1973, Building Structure Inventory Form prepared by the Friends of Historic Kingston records, "The original frame church which comprises the rear of the present building appears to be of the Greek Revival style. The church is approached by a double brick and bluestone stairway with wrought iron railings. The facade contains classical details. There is a broken pediment over the main doorway and Roman arch windows over the entrance. There is a round window in the pediment and two round windows on the second floor. All contain the Star of David. Windows contain diamond paned glass and there is a single doorway at either end of the main floor. It appears that the building served as a church then a synagogue and again as a church. This is the former synagogue Agudus Achim"; • that the applicant shall remodel the interior to accommodate two or three residential units, but that the remodeling shall not alter any exterior features that would compromise the structure's historical integrity, including but not limited to its fenestration, doorways, and wooden features; • that any HVAC units installed shall be subject to further review upon submission of additional information regarding their size, make, model, and location; • that the demolition of the small brick addition that housed the kitchen area and was not original to the structure is approved; • Any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; • The Commission's approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding amended findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 1 day of June 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (MG motion, RT-2nd, AP, KM, NM-yes)

The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application as presented and endorse the Preservation Notice of Action as adopted by the HLPC. (KM-motion, NM-2nd; JM, BH - yes)

items.title: #101 Broadway: Replace and reinforce existing roof, rebuild masonry parapets and chimneys, restore wooden windows and doors in-kind, improve site drainage, repair lower masonry and waterproofing
items.applicant: Reher Center for Immigrant Culture & History
items.owner: Reher Center for Immigrant Culture & History
items.discussion:
Marissa Marvelli on Behalf of the Reher Center, which is working with Preservationist
Architect Marylin Kaplan, presented the plans to restore the structure’s façade in-kind and to follow NPS
Standards and relevant Preservation Briefs. The work will include the replacement of the roof, masonry repairs,
window restoration by Emily Major of White Clay Kill Preservation, LLC, and woodwork, water control, and
the creation of one ADA accessible entry door via the Broadway side, that Marvelli assure the commission will
not alter the structure’s appearance.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed rehabilitation of the 1875 Italianate style structure at 99-101 Broadway in the Rondout Historic District by the Reher Center for Immigrant Culture & History, if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-64, of the City of Kingston's Administrative Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: • that the proposed work is to take place at the three-story Italianate (formerly mixed use) structure which according to the Friends of Historic Kingston’s July 15th, 1975, Building Structure Inventory form "is similar to 21-23 Broadway and dates to circa 1885. The structure does not appear on the 1870 Beers map of Rondout. The 2/2 windows remain, but the building has received major modern alterations, and that it is a contributory building in the district" and that more recently served as the place of business for the Reher Bakery; • that the applicant shall remove the existing roof, reinforce structural members, install new decking, flashing, and a new roof; • that the applicant shall repair and restore existing scuppers and downspouts to control the flow of water off of the roof; • that the applicant shall restore the existing chimneys and other masonry features in accordance with NPS Pres. Briefs 1 & 2; • that the parapets along the roof shall be restored in-kind; that all exterior woodwork shall be repaired/restored in-kind; • that all wooden windows and doors shall be restored in-kind by Emily Major of White Clay Kill Preservation, LLC; • that pending the issuing of necessary permits by DPW the applicant shall remove the sidewalk for the creation of better site drainage and for the repointing of the masonry foundation followed by the reinstallation of the bluestone sidewalk with replacement slabs as needed; • Any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; • The Commission's approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding amended findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 1st day of June 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (MC motion, RT-2nd, AP, KM, NM).

The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application as presented and endorse the Preservation Notice of Action as adopted by the HLPC. (KM-motion, JM-2nd; BH, NM - yes)

items.title: #95 Hone St: Repainting the structure’s exterior
items.discussion:
Jose Ramirez presented his plans (currently underway) of repainting 95 Hones Street from its
former blue to a new gold, green, and burgundy color scheme that according to him will differentiate it from
other structures within the neighborhood. He presently seeks retroactive approval for the portion of work
completed.  He also brought to the Commission his plans to alter the building design by moving/enlarging two
windows on the West Pierpont Street side of the structure.  As this work was not expressly identified in the
application, Mr. Ramirez was instructed to do some historic research and re-apply to the Commissions for the
window work.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed repainting of the exterior of the multi-unit dwelling at 95 Hones Street in the Rondout Historic District by Jose Ramirez, if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-64, of the City of Kingston's Administrative Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: • that the proposed work is to take place at the multi-unit 2.5 story three-sided bay Gothic Revival dwelling at the southwest corner of Hones and Pierpont Streets that according to the Friends of Historic Kingston's January 1977 Building-Structure Inventory Form informs us that "it is the only Gothic Revival house in this area - dating to circa 1890" and which does not appear on the 1880 Burleigh map of Kingston. The substantial house, which combines Gothic and Italianate features is interesting because of the late date of its construction. It retains its detailing and has received no major modern alterations on the exterior. However, the interior was gutted by a fire with the staircase being the only surviving original interior feature"; • that the applicant shall continue to paint the structure's body Benjamin Moore Mayan Gold 175 and Dorset Gold HC-8, with trim accents in Benjamin Moore Georgian Brick HC-50 and Turtle Green 2142-20; • that the applicant shall return to the Commission to discuss window replacement/addition; • Any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; • The Commission's approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies. Based on the preceding amended findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 1st day of June 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (NM motion, JM-2nd, MG, AP, KM-yes)

The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application as presented and endorse the Preservation Notice of Action as adopted by the HLPC. (NM-motion, JM-2nd; BH, KM - yes)

items.title: #14 Abeel St: Brush removal and new water drainage system, new asphalt roof and gutters, chimney and masonry wall and stairs restoration, in-kind wood repairs to porch, fascia, guard rail
items.discussion:
Andrea Puetz, Commissioner (recused), on behalf of SD Architects, presented the plans for
rehabilitating 14 Abeel Street. A. Puetz clarified that the asphalt shingle roof will be replaced in-kind.  All
masonry work will be done in-kind according to NPS standards.  A. Puetz noted that the chimneys will be
decommissioned and capped, but retained for the visual character, Paint colors have not yet been decided and
they will need to return for a review of those when determined,
Regarding the windows, A. Puetz stated that the majority of the structure’s windows are aluminum and appear
to have been replaced within the last 10 years. Not being original to the structure, it is the intention to replace
them with new wooden windows after submitting a Condition’s Assessment to the Commissions and receiving
their approval to move forward with replacement.  The plan includes the restoration of two existing wooden
oval windows located on the structure’s Gabel ends..

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed rehabilitation at 14 Abeel Street in the Rondout Historic District by 14 Abeel St, LLC, if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-64, of the City of Kingston's Administrative Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: • that the proposed work is to take place at the three bay, brick construction, two-story structure located at the northeastern end of Abeel St and which the Friends of Historic Kingston's July 15th, 1975, Building- Structure Inventory Form states " this Greek Revival residence dates between 1825- 1858 and appears on the 1858 French map of Ulster County. The exceptional structure retains almost all of its original elements and has received no major modern alterations. It is one of the best Greek Revival residences in the district"; • that the applicant shall replace the roof sections with in-kind materials as called for; • that the applicant shall repoint the masonry chimneys in accordance with NPS standards and the recommendations laid out in Preservation Brief 2; • that the applicant shall return to the commission with paint colors in the future; • that the applicant shall identify the age and document the existing conditions of the windows prior to return to the commission for approval for their replacement; • Any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; • The Commission's approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding amended findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 1st day of June, 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (MG motion, KM-2nd, NM, KM, RT-yes; AP recusal)

The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application as presented and endorse the Preservation Notice of Action as adopted by the HLPC. (KM-motion, NM-2nd; JM, BH - yes)

items.title: #80 Abeel St: Restore structure’s woodwork, chimneys, stairs, fire escape, siding; install new door; brush removal and drainage; roof and gutter replacement
items.discussion:
Andrea Puetz, Commissioner (recused), on behalf of SD Architects, presented plans for
rehabilitating 80 Abeel Street. A. Puetz submitted a statement which clarified that “1) The roofing is a mixture
of asphalt, bituminous, and possibly some standing seam metal. The asphalt roofing (unless a shallow roof) will
be replaced with new asphalt, bituminous will be replaced with EPDM (and shallow pitch roofs that were
asphalt), and the standing seam will be replaced with new standing seam. Colors have not been selected; we
will return with color selections at a future meeting. 2) Chimneys and masonry will use the appropriate type of
mortar for their intended application. Chimneys will be capped. 3) Paint colors for wood will be determined in
the future, we will return with final selections.”
The Commissions reviewed the overall proposed changes and restoration work.  The elevation plans were
discussed, and A. Puetz stated that the chimneys are being decommissioned, but retained for historic purposes.
Other work not mentioned in the email will be to repair the metal fire escape, by replacing landings and
scraping and painting the stairway surfaces.  The clapboard siding will be scraped, patched, and repaired
before new painting is done.  A table of new finishes is provided on the pan set to identify the various
treatments which will be undertaken and used.
M. Grunblatt noted the installation of newer doors to the rear of the property that are double French design,
out to rear patio areas.  These are not new openings but replacing and upgrading existing standard sliding
doors.
She noted that the number of units is increasing and an application for a special use permit is on file for review
by the Planning Board.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed exterior rehabilitation at 80 Abeel Street in the Rondout Historic District by Rian Bradley, if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-64, of the City of Kingston's Administrative Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: • that the proposed work is to take place at the four bay 2.5 story dwelling with a gable roof parallel to Abeel Street situated on the south side of Abeel street one property from the corner with Wurts Street, and which the Friends of Historic Kingston's November 5th, 1976 Building Structure Inventory Form states " this substantial residence appears on the 1870 Beers map of Rondout; it replaced a smaller structure (shown on the 1853 map) that was built into the front corner of the lot. The building, which belongs to no particular style, retains its 19th-century features, but it has received major modern alterations. It is a contributing building"; • that the applicant shall replace the existing roof with in-kind materials, with porch exception which will be EPDM cover; • that the applicant shall restore in-kind the existing masonry chimneys in accordance with NPS standards and the recommendations in NPS Pres. Brief 2; • that the applicant shall replace existing doors with French style sliding doors on the second rear floor; • that the applicant shall return to the Commission with colors to repaint the exterior of the structure; • that the applicant shall restore windows or return to discuss replacement of the existing windows; • Any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; • The Commission's approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding amended findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 1st day of June 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (MG motion, RT-2nd; NM, KM-yes; AP-recusal).

The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application as presented and endorse the Preservation Notice of Action as adopted by the HLPC. (JM-motion, NM-2nd; BH, KM - yes)

items.title: #57 North Front St: Install 2nd floor entryway, enlarge 2nd floor windows, addition of cornice on street front, alter storefront doors and windows, and paint façade
items.discussion:
Paul B. Jankovitz and Mr. DeCicco presented plans to rehabilitate 57 North Front Street which
was recently gutted by a fire. Their intention is to add a second-floor entryway on the northeastern side of the
street face to provide access to a second-floor apartment. They also seek approval to replace the existing 1/1
windows with two 6/1 windows separated by one 10/1 window. Staff explained to the Commissioners that this
alteration is not original as evidenced by historic photographs of the property. P. Jankovitz noted that they are

trying to incorporate more light into the interior space with the window changes and also to make the building
more attractive by installing a paneled cornice that is a reference to other structures in the uptown district. The
applicants informed the Commissions of their intention to paint the structure in Hardie Board Sandscript
SW1085 LRV 43% for the siding and Vineyard Green SW2244 for the cornice.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed restoration of the building at 57 North Front Street in the Stockade Historic District by Tana and Carmelo DeCicco, if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-64, of the City of Kingston's Administrative Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: • that the proposed work is required to restore an existing two-story storefront building recently damaged by a fire • that restoration will include the addition of a 2nd entryway to access the 2nd floor apartments, enlargement of the 2nd floor windows, addition of cornice on street front, alteration of storefront doors and windows, and painting the façade in Sandscript SW1085 LRV 43% for the siding and Vinyard Green SW2244 for the cornice; • Any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; • The Commission's approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding amended findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 1st day of June 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (MG motion, KM-2nd; AP, JM, RT-yes)

The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application as presented and endorse the Preservation Notice of Action as adopted by the HLPC. (KM-motion, NM-2nd; BH, JM - yes)

items.title: #317 Wall St: Restore two storefront in-filled windows
items.discussion:
Paul B. Jankovitz on behalf of 317 Wall Street, LLC, presented the plan to restore two brick
infilled storefront windows beneath the Pike Plan. P. Jankovitz assured the Commissioners and Staff that
behind the walls are the original windows and frame in good condition. The windows sit atop small knee wall
that will be exposed.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed restoration of two storefront in-filled windows at 317 Wall Street in the Stockade Historic District by 317 Wall Street LLC, if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-64, of the City of Kingston's Administrative Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: • that the proposed work is to take place at an existing two-story storefront building constructed in 1973; • that the work will include restoration of two storefront windows that were previously filled in with masonry • Any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; • The Commission's approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding amended findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 1st day of June 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (MG motion, KM-2nd; AP, JM, NM-yes)

The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application as presented and endorse the Preservation Notice of Action as adopted by the HLPC. (NM-motion, KM-2nd; JM, BH - yes).

items.title: #328 Wall St: Installation of canvas 22’ long x 4’ wide canopy over entry door and street face
items.discussion:
Paul B. Jankovitz and Myron Mishell, on behalf of Magic Hill, presented to the Commissions
their intention to install an awning over the entrance and window of the Fair Street side of 328 Wall Street. An
existing modern window on the ground floor shall be replaced with a sliding service window for the business
to sell its products to customers on the street. The applicant also seeks to install a small shelf or counter at the
window’s base for condiments, napkins, et.al. and cited the neighboring Stockade Bar for their countertop.
Staff were not in favor of permanent counter as it presents an obstruction for pedestrians. The applicant agreed
to recessing the window to create a shelf or to use a shelf that can fold down after business hours.  A final
design will be submitted for staff review before installation.   Lastly, the applicant intends to return to the
Commissions for approval to repaint the structure.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed installation of a canvas canopy over the entry door and street face at 328 Wall Street in the Stockade Historic District by 328 Wall Street LLC, if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-64, of the City of Kingston's Administrative Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: • that the proposed work is to take place at an existing 3 story storefront building which, according to the Building Inventory Form, is thought to be constructed in or around the 1850's • that the work will include the installation of a 22' x 4' canvas canopy over the existing entry door and street face and will extend over a portion of the City right of way requiring submission of insurance naming the City as additionally insured; • Any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; • The Commission's approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding amended findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 1st day of June 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (MG motion, KM-2nd; AP, NM, RT-yes)

The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application as presented and endorse the Preservation Notice of Action as adopted by the HLPC. (JM-motion, KM-2nd; BH, NM - yes)

items.title: #322 Wall St: Window replacement and exterior painting
items.discussion:
The applicant was not present. Staff explained that this project is partially funded by an
Uptown Façade grant program. The applicant seeks to repaint the structure and to either restore or replace
windows on the second and third floor of the Wall Street face. Staff reviewed the photos provided by the
applicant of windows and believe they are restorable. The applicant has provided an image of a replacement
window for the larger second story window, but has not provided the maker, model, and specifications. Staff
also noted that there is no documentation provided for the conditions of the existing windows and
recommends that this aspect be held over for further review until that information and documentation can be
provided.
The paint colors for the building were reviewed, with no further discussion.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed exterior painting at 322 Wall Street in the Stockade Historic District by Geddy Sveikoukas, if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-64, of the City of Kingston's Administrative Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: • that the proposed work is to take place at an existing 3 story storefront building constructed in the mid 1800's • that the project includes restoration and painting of the façade in a Birch Bark D22-1 and trim with Gris de Boothbay HC-165 as presented; • that authorization for replacement of the 2nd and 3rd floor windows is withheld for submission of a completed conditions assessment documenting the current state of the windows. Said report to be completed by a professional preservationist. The HLPC notes that restoration is preferred to replacement; • Any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; • The Commission's approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding amended findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 1st day of June 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (MG motion, KM-2nd; AP, NM, RT-yes)

The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application as presented and endorse the Preservation Notice of Action as adopted by the HLPC. (JM-motion, KM-2nd; BH, NM - yes)

items.title: #77 Main St: Installation of rooftop mounted solar panels
items.discussion:
Amanda LaValle and R. Countryman, of Solar Generation of Kingston presented the plan to
install 24 Silfab 380-watt DC Solar Panels totaling 9.1kW on the south facing street roof of the mid-century
ranch office building adjacent to the 1728 Jacob Elmendorf House. With the exception to the panels, no lines or
equipment shall be visible from the street. A new conduit shall be installed on the north side of the Elmendorf
House to replace the existing lines which are exposed. The new conduit will be treated to match the existing
color of the structure.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed installation of rooftop mounted solar panels at 77 Main Street in the Stockade Historic District, if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-64, of the City of Kingston's Administrative Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: • that the proposed work is to take place on the 1950's addition of a historic home dating believed to have been constructed a short time after the Revolution. The home originally belonged to Jacob Elmendorf with the addition constructed and used as a doctor's office since its ownership of A.W. Hazenbush. • that the work includes installation by Solar Generation of Kingston, NY for 24 Silfab 380-watt DC Solar Panels totaling 9.1kW mounted on the roof; • that the new electrical conduit on the 18th-century dwelling shall be painted to match the exterior of the 18th-century dwelling; • Any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; • The Commission's approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding amended findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 1st day of June 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (MG motion, NM-2nd; AP, KM, RT-yes)

The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application as presented and endorse the Preservation Notice of Action as adopted by the HLPC. items.title: Adoption of the Minutes of June 1st, 2023, Meeting: a. HAC Adoption of the Minutes of June 1st, 2023, Meeting:
#68 St. James Street: Window replacements
items.discussion:
The owner, Anne Stedge Outwater and Melissa Sedwick, representative of Home Depot,
presented plans to replace 9 windows on the third-floor apartment of the structure along the Clinton Avenue
and St James Street faces. M. Sedwick noted that the existing windows that are being replaced are all currently
vinyl and have exterior storms.  The applicant provided staff with photographs of the structure from street
level and a drawing that loosely identified the locations of the third story windows. The proposed replacement
windows are Simonton 6500 Series style, vinyl, in the color white.  Because there will not be separate exterior
components, the owner stated that she believed the newer windows will have an overall more appealing,
cleaner look than present.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application to replace 9 windows on the third floor of the structure with Simonton 6500 series, vinyl windows in white. (JM-motion, MD-2nd, BH, NM, KM-yes).

items.title: #16-18 Gill Street: Installation of HVAC unit and fence
items.discussion:
The applicant, Karolina Hart, is seeking retroactive approval for the installation of an HVAC
condenser on the northwest (playground) side of 16-18 Gill Street visible from the street. She stated that they
will treat the condenser and lines that run on the exterior wall of the structure the same color as the structure,
noting that she was before the Commission earlier and a dark green color was approved.  The HAC discussed
how the condenser unit was secured    and K. Hart stated that it was secured with brackets that are affixed to
the masonry wall of the building.
K. Hart also stated that they are proposing to construct a wooden fence that will serve to create a visual, sound,
and privacy barrier between the playground and the structure. The applicant stated they will paint the fence to
match the structure’s black trim. The fencing will extend along the side yard abutting the playground and a
gate will be placed along the street.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the installation of a solid wooden fence that will be treated black along the side yard and street frontage, with a gate; along with the retroactive approval of the installation of the HVAC condenser unit and associated lines, painted in a dark green to match the new paint on the exterior. (JM-motion, MD-2nd, BH, NM, KM-yes).

items.title: #600 Aaron Court: Installation of 1,186 PV panels, across 6 buildings, mounted on flat roofs

items.discussion:
Seth Walker, Greenleaf Solar, presented the plan to install a low-profile solar system at the
Aaron Court office building complex, consisting of 1,186 panels. The applicant will use EcoFoot2+ Ballasted
Racking System PV panels on the flat roofs of six structures at Aaron Court. S. Walker stated that the panels
will not be visible due to the parapet surrounds on the roofs of all the buildings.  When asked about the
reflective potential, he explained that the panels are coated so that they will not produce a glare for
neighboring buildings and residents.

Patrick Casey, Architect from Andrade Architecture, presented the Commission the plans to
rehabilitate the exterior and second floor balcony of 718 Broadway.  The building currently functions as
Broadway Bubbles Laundromat on the ground floor and an office space on the second floor. The applicant
intends to upgrade the second-floor façade which faces Broadway. The Commission confirmed the current use
of the second-floor space is not changing. The work includes replacing the existing anodized sliding glass doors
with anodized aluminum windows and a single door located at the southeastward end of the deck made by
Kolbe VistaLuxe Collection Finish. P. Casey reviewed an elevation of the building that distinguished between
the existing and proposed features.  He noted that removing all the door openings improved space functionality
on the interior and provided for a better layout of the balcony.  Four Tolson Caged Wall Sconces from
Rejuvenation Finish, Oil Rubbed Bronze will be installed between the windows and door to illuminate the
second story deck. Staff stated that the new lighting is far enough off the street that it will most likely not
cause any issue.  However, it was noted that should it become a problem, staff can work with the owner to
correct.  The applicant also intends to remove the existing plywood cornice and clean and repair in-kind the
façade. As shown on the proposed renderings for the structure, a new smaller cornice will be installed and
painted green to match the structure’s other trim. P. Casey identified 2 railing styles for the balcony and asked
for the HAC opinion on which to use.  The HAC unanimously agreed that the industrial style 42” tall railing
should be installed on the second-floor balcony, with an anodized aluminum finish.  Finally, the applicant
intends to add a pull-out Sunesta retractable awning in green on the second story over the deck and will redo
the existing decking with Tile Tech IPE on Pedestal system with a weathered finish. A product sample of the
flooring was presented for the Commissioner’s to see the material.  Planters will also be included on the second
story behind the railing.

Tyson McCasland of Timely Signs of Kingston presented plans to replace the existing signage
for Broadway Bubble with new signs that shall mount in the same locations.  He stated that presently there are
temporary signs that are in place and the new signs will be more consistent with the new façade and site
improvements.  T. McCasland provided the Commissioner’s with handouts to show the new signage.
• One 68” wide (X) 80” tall (X) ¾” thick sign with ½” PVC accents on the structure’s tower.
• Two 96” wide (X) 37” tall acrylic face signs with printed vinyl applied and installed in the existing pylon
sign at the street, perpendicular to Broadway.
The signs shall be direct replacements. The signs mounted in the pylon shall have internal illumination and the
applicant has agreed to install a timer so that the sign turns off when the business is not active.

The applicant, Tom Kreuger, was absent but has submitted photographs and color samples for
review and approval by the HAC and HLPC. T Kreuger seeks approval to paint the exterior trim Sussex Green
from the Benjamin Moore Historical Collection and that the masonry shall be painted Castleton Mist from the
Benjamin Moore Historic Collection. Staff reviewed the proposed colors and find that they conform with the
structure’s design and historical character. While the structure was originally white on white, this two-color
scheme will enhance the structure’s features and add to the streetscape. Recognizing these colors will alter the
structure’s appearance, the applicant has brought it to the Commissions for their review and approval.

Angel Lopez,  the contractor hired by owner James Evans, presented  the proposal to install a
new railing on the front porch of the dwelling that will include turned wooden balustrades at evenly spaced
intervals. While not original to the structure, as indicated by historical photographs of the property, the
Commissioners acknowledged that child safety is imperative and that the railings could be removed in the
future, and for these reasons the project is permissible.

The owner is seeking retroactive approval for work that was undertaken without either
Commissions review.  Christopher Konoski presented the work that he did to 81 W. Pierpont Street between
September 2019 and the present, which included the following:
• Removing the first-floor leftmost front window and install new door as new point of egress for the first
floor, paint blue (Paint color: Benjamin Moore - symphony Blue - 2060-10 or similar);
• removing the current entranceway screen door, replace current entryway door and use as second floor point
of egress, paint yellow (Paint color: Benjamin Moore - Banana yellow - 2022-41or similar);
• installing Vinyl siding on original house structure, color blue (Paint color: Benjamin Moore - Symphony
Blue - 2060-10 or similar);
• installing Stucco siding on front house extension and 8 ft of the side of house extension, color gray (Paint
color: Benjamin Moore - Nickel - 2j.19-50 or similar);
• installing vinyl window shutters on second floor front three windows, color white (paint color: Benjamin
Moore - lcicle - 2142-70 or similar);
• replacing the current cement entry stairs with wood stairs and stain gray (Stain color: Behr - Cape Cod
Gray - 5T365 or similar);
• install new wood stairway for new entrance and stain gray (Stain color: Behr - Cape Cod Gray - 5T365 or
similar);
• removal of the side entryway and move to rear of house;
• removal of the basement entryway and fill opening for a paved walkway;
• installation of a new vinyl soffit on all four sides of house, color white (paint color: Benjamin Moore - icicle

- 2142-70 or similar);
He stated that all the work was completed with Building permits, and he had P. Jankovitz as his architect.  He
stated that he was told that the Commission’s reviews were only advisory.  Staff stated that even so, that didn’t
authorize work to proceed without consulting the Commissions.  Perhaps, alternative materials would have
been encouraged, resulting in a project that more closely resembled the character of the area.  While the
structure is not within the boundary of the Historic District, it does reflect on and has a role in complimenting
the district.  The Commission make very effort to keep the essence of the architecture ever present.  Staff noted
that a check on Municity (software that the city uses) did not reveal the necessary permits and that the matter
would best be tabled until the paperwork could be researched, and Corporation Counsel could be consulted
for an opinion.

Lisa G. Collins & Lee A. Bernstein (owners) and Edgar Lee, contactor, presented plans to
repair and replace in-kind wooden clapboard siding and trim that has degraded and paint the structure. Wood
shall be replaced with wood. Once replaced the structure shall be repainted in Benjamin Moore Prussian Blue
CW-625 and Benjamin Moore tout gray 2124-20. According to the applicants it is the desire to paint the entire
house, including the trim, with tout gray 2124-20 and the front entrance will be the only feature painted
Prussian Blue CW-625. Staff notes that while the blue is a color choice to accent the doorway, it should stay
there alone, but suggested that a slightly different color gray could be used to accent the doorway architectural
framework.  It was discussed that a similar hue, maybe a slight shade different from the body color be used to
help set off the doorway.  The applicants indicated that they would consider but were not ready to sign on to
that.  They asked if they could have time to decide.

Matt Stauffer , represented the owner.  He presented the plan to repaint 316 Wall Street, also
including the Fair Street face following the existing color scheme using Benjamin Moore HS Hancock Green for
the primary/body color and Benjamin Moore Off White Collection Ice Mist for the trim on Wall and using the
BM Off white, for Fair Street, including the proposed bulkhead (defined as a staircase).

Paul Jankovitz, Architect, and Tyson McCasland, of Timely Signs, represented both applicants
and owners.  P. Jankovitz reviewed the proposal for the City of Kingston Library’s to temporarily relocate to
this location while renovations take place at their facility.  To accommodate the library, exterior rehabilitation
of 61 Crown Street (the former City of Kingston School District’s Administrative Building) is necessary. The
library expects to be in the structure for approximately 18 months while they undertake significant renovations
to their facility on Franklin Street. P. Jankovitz, reviewed the aspects of the plan including repairs to parking
lot, restriping of parking areas, repairs/repointing to brick walls along Crown Street and Green Street (which
as of Friday, June 30th already began). He noted that under this project they will be installing two EV Charging
stations visible from Green Street, and which would be near the north-south lot-line with the private residence
to the immediate south of 61 Crown Street. There are also plans to upgrade and add lighting updates to the
property. At least two light poles will be located south of the EV charging stations. P. Jankovitz noted that they
will be in Contact with the adjacent landowner to work with them on lighting so that possibly both entities
may benefit from the improvements.  The Commissions asked about how the wall packs would be installed and
P. Jankovitz noted that the fixtures are being installed where there are current lights, they are not intended to
be permanent.  When they return for future use of the property, more period style fixtures, that are decorative
and compatible with a building development plan will be chosen.
T. McCasland, reviewed the signage.  Timely Signs of Kingston will be producing and installing two identical
signs, one on the Crown and other on the Green Street sides of the property. The signs will be 43” high by 50”
wide, white with maroon and black coloring. The signs’ text will read, “Temporary Home of The Kingston
Library, established 1899.” No lighting is planned.  They are intentionally not affixing the signage to the brick
walls as they are only temporary.
A black aluminum fence will replace the existing chain-link fence along the driveway which enters from Crown
Street. On Crown Street side there are masonry walls that also serve as planters. The applicant intends to plant

Boxwood and Rhododendrons there, and several Eastern Arborvitae on the northwesternmost corner of the
property along Green Street.
P. Jankovitz, noted that last, the applicant is proposing to perform repairs to roof gutters and to repaint

items.title: Adoption of the Minutes of July 6th, 2023, Meeting: a. HAC Adoption of the Minutes of July 6th, 2023, Meeting:
#30 Sycamore Street: Construction of a shed in back yard
items.discussion:
The applicant and owner, Katrina Simpson, presented the Commission her plans to construct a
16’x16’ shed in her back yard and landscape her property along her lot lines. She noted that she is a designer by
trade and that she wishes to use native plantings around the property and that she will use a portion of the
shed for storage and some for workspace.  She makes this location her full-time residence.  Several shrubs will
be planted in the earth between the sidewalk and her fence along Sycamore Street and additional shrubbery
throughout the backyard. The Commission discussed the use of planters and encroaching on the public right of
way.  K. Simpson indicated she had a survey and would not use the planters along the roadway, instead just
adding landscaping directly in the ground.  Fencing will be installed along the backyard lot lines to increase
privacy and to screen the shed.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application to install fencing along the property’s front and rear lot lines, landscaping, and the construction of a 16’x 16’ shed in the property’s rear, recognizing that the planters are removed from the design and landscaping will be placed directly in the ground along the street frontage out of the public right-of way. (JM-motion, KM-2nd, all-yes).

items.title: #636 Broadway: Wall, window, and overhanging signage & façade painting
items.discussion:
The applicant, Nick Africano, and his business partner, Harry McNamara, presented to the
commission plans for updating the first-floor street facing façade of 636 Broadway in anticipation for their new
Andalusian Restaurant, “Mirador”. The applicant was questioned about the total signage being over busy and
repetitive. Commissioners also discussed if the gate was part of the application as it was unclear, and if it was
necessary for the project.  H. McNamara stated that the gate was something that they could do without for the
present time but wanted to continue with the signage as proposed.    N. Africano explained that while there is a
certain degree of repeated information, the overall dimensions are not out of line with the space.  He noted that
the projecting sign, internally illuminated, would not have text, but a logo only for recognition.  Staff advised
that if the Commission authorized the projecting sign there would be a clearance requirement and also
insurance naming the city as additionally insured.  The applicant agreed to secure insurance for their projecting
sign and list the City of Kingston as co-insured.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application for signage in the windows, on the wall, and projecting sign, noting that the gate would not be installed at the present time, and that the projecting sign would maintain a minimum of 8 ‘ clearance from grade and that the applicants will provide the city with insurance naming the City as additionally insured in accordance with §358-9 of the City Code. (JM-motion, KM-2nd, all-yes).

items.title: #728 Broadway: Exterior modifications, windows, & signage
items.discussion:
The applicant, Andrea Gamalski, owner and Steven Crews, contractor for owner, presented to
the Commission her plans to restore mid-20th-century art deco-like façade of 728 Broadway. The applicant does
not intend to alter the façade’s appearance at all.  However, due to the condition of the materials, the existing
green and chrome panels will be replaced with stainless steel panels of the same size, powder coated to match
the existing color scheme. The green panels and coloring will extend from the front façade along the northwest
side of the building, approximately halfway back.  The chrome edging will also be completely replaced with
new materials.

The existing signage will be restored in-kind and illuminated via simple neon lighting and is being restored by
Lite Brite Neon of Kingston.  The signage would only identify the property address and the overall appearance
of the building would be brought back to an earlier era.  There is no window signage included with the
application.  However, they do plan to replace all the storefront windows with double pane glass for energy
savings.

Staff advised that the clearance is pre-existing, and that insurance is required naming the city as additionally
insured.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application to restore the existing storefront and to replace the existing panels with stainless painted to match the existing color scheme, restore the overhanging signage to have the building identification and that the applicant will provide the city with insurance naming the City as additionally insured in accordance with §358-9 of the City Code. . (NM-motion, KM-2nd, all-yes).

items.title: #49 Lindsley Avenue: Installation of 5.6 kW roof mounted solar array with 14 panels and supporting equipment
items.discussion:
The applicant, Charles Winchell, and Ryan Schumacher of Plug PV, presented to the
commission their plans to install 14 solar panels totaling 5.6 kW on the roof of 49 Lindsley Avenue. The
applicant took the position that the panels will not adversely impact the structure’s appearance, as they are
located on the roof and do not have a steep angle to them.  Additionally, they are planning to treat both the
lines and the box covering the side mounted equipment to match the color of the existing siding.  Staff noted
that due to the presence of the existing utility service and the driveway, no other means of screening, or other
suitable location are possible without extensive reconfiguring the services.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application to install 14 solar panels totaling 5.6 kW on the roof of 49 Lindsley Avenue and to treat the lines and equipment to match the structure’s existing color by Plug PV of Troy, NY (JM-motion, NM-2nd, all-yes).
