items.title: #106-122 Green Street: Replacement of all windows
items.discussion:
NOTE: Commissioner Grunblatt recused himself from the meeting as he has an interest in an
adjoining property.  He left the table and Commissioner McEvoy, took over the role a HLPC Chairman for the
matter.
The applicant, Selina Guendel on behalf of the Wiltwyck Chapter of the NSDAR, returned to the commissions
seeking approval to replace all the existing wooden windows on their structure at 106-122 Green Street. The
applicant confirmed they received from staff and reviewed an updated window condition assessment
documenting the interior and exterior conditions of the existing windows, which was drafted by staff after
attending a site visit with some Commission members on July 10, 2023. The applicant had no additional
information to share but did clarify that the application at hand only focused on the windows and that the
shutters were not part of the application at this time. Staff noted that the report had been circulated amongst
all members of both Commissions and asked if anyone had any comments or questions regarding the content or
with the application.  It was noted that no new information had been submitted and that staff provided notes
with recommendations and references to other projects in advance of the meeting to members.
Hearing no further discussion, Acting Chairman McEvoy undertook a SEQR Determination which is identified
in the below decision.  He then proceeded to read into the record a proposed motion to approve the application
for replacing the windows on the site.  No second was submitted by any member of the HLPC, and the motion
failed.  The decision went forth as follows.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the replacement of the existing windows at 106-122 Green Street in the Stockade Historic District by the Wiltwyck Chapter of the NSDAR, if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and prior meetings, that according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-26, of the City of Kingston's Form Based Code, is not compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: • that the proposed work is to take place at the 2.5 story Georgian almost square, block with an extension to the rear - is believed to have been built between 1660 and 1695 by Anthony Crispell. At some point, the property's owners Georgianized the structure to conform with contemporary social and architectural trends. By the time of the American Revolution, it was owned by Henry (Hendrick) Sleight and was burned in 1777. It is reported that General Washington, Governor Clinton, the Tappens, Sleights, and the Wynkoops are related to this dwelling. The structure was rebuilt in 1794 by John Tappen, a lawyer, who was editor and proprietor of the Ulster Plebian, a Democrat newspaper of the early 19th-century. It was said to have been printed on the second floor of the house from 1813 until his death. A book and stationary store were also operated out of the structure in the lower front corner room along Green Street. In 1907, the house was purchased by the Wiltwyck Chapter of the Daughters of the American Revolution and has been maintained as a museum since then. (Information sourced from the March 3rd, 1974, and July 1987 Building- Structure Inventory form housed on NYS State Historic Preservation Office's digital Cultural Resource Information System.); • that documentation and evidence provided by the owner/applicant is not sufficient to demonstrate that the existing historic wooden windows are beyond repair and that replacing the existing windows is the only option; • that a site visit was conducted on July 10, 2023, and Commissioners and staff in attendance observed and found the existing windows to be in restorable condition, a material reality that runs contrary to the position held by the applicant and shared with the commission since 2022; • that based on said site inspection, comprehensive review of application materials and documents provided, and US Secretary of Interior Standards for Rehabilitation, the City's Historic Preservation Administrator prepared a Window Assessment Report to document conditions and the HLPC has had the opportunity to review and consider that document; • that the existing windows must be restored to maintain the structure's historical integrity; • that the applicant/owner shall engage a qualified historic preservation professional, approved by the city staff, to undertake and complete the restoration work in accordance with industry standards and the using the US Secretary of Interior Preservation Briefs as a guide; • that the owner shall initiate a regular schedule of maintenance going forward to continue the condition standards; • any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described in this determination will be subject to further review by the Historic Landmarks Preservation Commission prior to the work being carried out; • that the Commission's directive for restoration over removal does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 24th day of August, 2023, the Commission DENY the request for window replacement and GRANT a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for window restoration work as described herein, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (MG -recuse; KM-motion, RT-2nd, all others-yes).

The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to deny the application to replace the existing wooden windows and to support the HLPC’s Preservation Notice of Action as approved. (NM-motion, KM-2nd, all-yes).

items.title: #95 Hone Street: Relocation and replacement of windows, installation of HVAC and site work
items.discussion:
The applicant, Jose Ramirez, and Michael Christman (executor for former owner Darrell
Christman) presented to the commissions the plans to remove the small second story window of the north half
of the west facing side of 95 hone street and to replace it with the original wooden window taken from the
south side of the same level on the western facing wall. The southern second story west facing window will be
reduced in size slightly to accommodate the interior space’s usage as a kitchen. On the first floor of the same
west facing wall, the small southern window will be expanded to add light into the new kitchen area. As a
window replacement project, the Commissioners discussed the age and condition of the windows being
changed and enlarged.  M. Christman stated that his father had installed the smaller windows around 1972
when he owned the property, to accommodate some interior alterations which he was making.  Photographs of
the windows had been submitted and the Commissioners found that the window changes were acceptable as
the window style, form, and trim will be retained.
The Commissions then reviewed the other site work being proposed as general improvements, including the
use of Belgian block as a pervious area in the driveway, removal of a storage shed, repair of the rear porch,
adding new pavement for the parking area incorporating a new dry stack stone wall at the rear, planting
shrubbery to add some green landscaping, resetting the flagstone pathways to provide even walks on site, and
installing HVAC units with a wooden screening.  Overall, the Commissioners were pleased with the sitework
planned and or completed as improving the general appearance of the site.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed window replacement and modification, HVAC condenser installation, and site work at 95 Hone Street in the Rondout Historic District by owner Jose Ramirez, if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in under Section 405-26, of the City of Kingston's Form Based Code, is partially compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: • that the proposed work is to take place at the multi-unit 2.5 story three-sided bay Gothic Revival dwelling at the southwest corner of Hone and Pierpont Streets that according to the Friends of Historic Kingston's January 1977 Building-Structure Inventory Form informs us that "it is the only Gothic Revival house in this area - dating to circa 1890" and which does not appear on the 1880 Burleigh map of Kingston. The substantial house, which combines Gothic and Italianate features is interesting because of the late date of its construction. It retains its detailing and has received no major modern alterations on the exterior. However, the interior was gutted by a fire with the staircase being the only surviving original interior feature"; • that the applicant has demonstrated that the proposed first and second floor window modifications and replacements are necessary and therefore shall be undertaken; • that the applicant shall install two HVAC units on the southeastward face of the structure near the rear porch & entryway with wooden screening; • that the applicant shall remove the existing plastic shed and plant shrubs along the property line; • that the existing asphalt driveway shall be repaved, sloping to direct drainage for collection on-site; • that the applicant has installed a Belgian block apron inside the property line and adjacent to the bluestone sidewalk; • that the applicant may construct a dry stack stone retaining wall at the eastern end of the driveway and a mortared retaining wall that will run along the driveway near the house; • that the applicant will reset all flagstone walkways; • that any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; • that the Commission's approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding amended findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 24th day of August 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (MG-motion, AP-2nd, all-yes).

The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application to replace two windows and modify three on the westward face of 95 Hone, installation of two HVAC condensers, site modifications, and landscape restoration as presented. (NM-motion, JM-2nd, all-yes).

items.title: #81 West Pierpont Street: Retroactive approval of siding, window alterations and removal, and construction of a cornice and porch
items.discussion:
The applicant was not present.  The project was tabled last month to allow for further review
by staff with Corporation Counsel.  Staff stated that the applicant did not return for review of the exterior
work as was requested of them by both Commissions in 2019, and that the Building and Safety Division
mistakenly approved a building permit for the work without recognizing that HAC & HLPC review was
needed on an advisory level and determinations were pending. Staff recognizes that errors were made by both
parties and that pursuing restoration is not appropriate at this time. It was recommended that the work be
acknowledged, without a formal approval, noting that both Commissions would not have approved the
alterations that took place, and a clear statement that the owner come to the Planning Department and the
Historic Preservation Administrator prior to undertaking future work that could result in alterations to the
structure’s exterior.  R. Tonner noted that he was disappointed but recognizes that the role of both
Commission’s would only be advisory given the property is just outside the historic district boundaries.  He
asked how to avoid this situation going forward.  Staff noted that the lines of communication have improved,
and decisions of the agencies are sent to multiple parties to ensure that awareness is heightened.
Staff provided a draft of a communication for both Commissions to consider in place of a formal decision
document.  The drafted letter reads as follows:

Dear Mr. Konoski:
This letter is to advise you that at the regular meeting of the Historic Landmarks Preservation Commission (HLPC) held on
August 24th, 2023, the Commission unanimously determined the application referenced above to be a Type II action under SEQRA,
and unanimously voted to retroactively recognize project elements with the following components understood:

• that the proposed work is to take place at the two bay, two-story structure with the gable end facing West Pierpont Street, and
which is located on the north side of West Pierpont mid-way between McEntee and Hone Streets, which according to the
photographs stored in the City of Kingston's Assessor's Office likely served as a single or multi-unit dwelling since at least the
1950s and which appears on the 1887 Sanborn map, having been built before then, possibly a reconstruction of a building
appearing on the same lot on the 1870 Beers Map of Rondout, Kingston, and Wilbur;
• that according to the September 2019 HLPC and HAC determinations, the applicant was supposed to have returned with
greater detail of the colors, materials, and design to the Planning Staff for review and approval and that the applicant
knowingly did not do as requested of them;
• that the City of Kingston’s Building and Safety Division mistakenly approved the applicant’s permit application on September
20th, 2020, without confirming either the HAC nor HLPC’s determination;
• that the HAC & HLPC would not have approved the applicant’s proposed alterations if the applicant had returned to the
Commissions;
• that the applicant must contact the Planning Department for advisement and review before undertaking any future projects
that might alter the structure’s exterior appearance.

Thank you for your time and cooperation.

decisions.text: The Historic Landmarks Preservation Commission (HLPC) voted unanimously to accept the drafted letter and authorize staff to send to the applicant, with a copy to the Building Safety Division. (MG – motion, NM – 2nd, all yes)

The Heritage Area Commission (HAC) voted unanimously to accept the drafted letter and authorize staff to send to the applicant, with a copy to the Building Safety Division. (BH-motion, KM-2nd, all- yes).

items.title: #322 Wall Street: Window replacement/restoration
items.discussion:
Genia Wickwire, representing the owner, presented the plans to restore three third story
windows and replace one large bay window at 322 Wall Street. The materials submitted included a report from
Kurt Riegel of Riegel Restoration’s.  The assessment identified that the second story window is not historic, in
disrepair, and could be replaced without advisedly impacting the structure’s integrity. Additionally, the report
clarifies that the third story windows are original and should be restored.  Commissioners reviewed the
information and noted that the photos and documentation submitted was acceptable to demonstrate that the
project should move forward, incorporating both a restoration component for windows on the third level and
replacement for the second story.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed window replacement and exterior painting at 322 Wall Street in the Stockade Historic District by Geddy Sveikoukas, if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-26, of the City of Kingston's Form-Based Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: • that the proposed work is to take place at an existing 3 story storefront building constructed in the mid 1800's; • that applicant has produced a window condition assessment by Kurt Riegel of Riegel Restoration a historic wood window specialist from Sydney, NY, which satisfactorily demonstrated that the large second floor window is not original to the structure, in disrepair, and cannot be salvaged and that the third story's 6 over 6 wooden windows are original and can and should be restored; • that the applicant may replace the existing second story window with a window type approved by staff, but must restore the third story wooden windows, engaging a historic preservation professional to undertake the work in accordance with the US Secretary of Interior Standards for Rehabilitation; • that the owner will engage in a regular maintenance program once restoration is complete to continue the condition standards; • that any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; • that the Commission's approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding amended findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 24th day of August 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (MG-motion, AP-2nd, All-yes).

The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application to restore three historic wooden windows on the third floor and to replace one non- historic and degraded window on the second story Wall Street face (JM-motion, KM-2nd, all-yes).

items.title: #61 Crown Street: Painting wooden trim
items.discussion:
P. Jankovitz, Architect, representing the owner, presented the proposal to paint the wooden
trim of 61 Crown Street white which they have identified was the original color through a historic postcard and
from scrapping the trim to reveal earlier paint layers. Commissioners and staff found that using white for the
trim was more defining for the building.  K. McEvoy stated that he has seen the white which is in place as the
basecoat, and it is appropriate.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed exterior modifications for the 18-month temporary relocation of the Kingston Library, located at 61 Crown Street in the Stockade Historic District, owned by 61 Crown Street LLC, if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-26, of the City of Kingston's Form-Based Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: • that the proposed work is to take place at the two- and one-half story former City of Kingston School District's administrative building, known as the Cioni Building, which stands mid-way between North Front and John Streets, and which also fronts to Green Street to the west; • that the applicant is permitted to paint the structure's exterior wooden trim in Sherwin Williams SW 7004 Snowbound (white); • that any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; • that the Commission's approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding amended findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 24th day of August 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (MG-motion, KM-2nd, all-yes).
The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application to Sherwin Williams SW 7004 Snowbound (white). (JM-motion, KM-2nd, all-yes).

items.title: #135 Hunter Street: Waterproofing basement, repointing masonry walls, painting, & site work
items.discussion:
Owner/Applicant, Dylan Kaplowitz, presented plans for rehabilitating 135 Hunter Street – a
property he inherited from his father. D. Kaplowitz, intends to repoint the structure, construct a new
historically sensitive entryway, install a French drain around the perimeter of the structure, construct a 6’ fence
in the back yard, and interior renovations to turn it into a two family – owner occupied – dwelling.
Commission members present discussed how well the structure seems to have been preserved.  D. Kaplowitz
noted that his father took pride in working on the structure and that he had replaced the front doors.  The
staircase he is proposing will have a larger landing than the entryway for safety reasons, but at the present time
he does not intend to rebuild an entire front porch as historically stood in place.  The front stairs will not have a
covering, but the Commissioners did recommend that the staircase railings and balustrades be chosen with
similar features to others in the area that are more decorative.  Looking at what was on the front porch may not
be appropriate for the staircase, and wrought iron had been historically in place, so staff will be authorized to
work with the owner to come to a solution. Staff and A. Puetz noted that the identified light fixture did not fit
with the architecture and recommended that the applicant work with staff to provide something more in
conformity with the building style and age.  The balance of the proposed improvements was found to be
acceptable to the Commissions.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that Introducing the motion that the Commissioners present find as fact that the proposed facade repointing, front porch repairs, installation of a fence, and structural support to the foundation at 135 Hunter Street, in the Rondout Historic District, by Dylan Kaplowitz, if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-26, of the City of Kingston's Form-Based Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: • that the proposed work is to take place at the 2 and 1/2 story with basement brick dwelling with its gable end facing Hunter Street and which is located at the north corner of the intersection of Hunter and Ravine Street and which according to the January 1977 Building Structure Inventory Form, produced by the Friends of Historic Kingston states "this residence appears on the 1870 Beers map of Rondout. The gable- fronted structure retains some of its major features, but its facade has received major modern alterations. It is a contributory building in the district." • that the entryway's frame shall be painted Benjamin Moore Distant Gray OC-68 and the entryway's double door will be painted Benjamin Moore Essex Green HC-188; • that the applicant shall be permitted to install a stain-glass transom window to replace the existing single pane clear glass window; • that the entryway stairs and railing shall be rebuilt of wood and painted white, with design elements to be determined with staff which are reflective of local community neighborhood area; • that the entry light fixture will be changed in consultation with staff to a more appropriate period style fixture for architecture of building; • that the applicant shall construct a 5ft tall fence in the rear yard for screening and to protect their animals which will be made of horizontal wooden boards that will be stained for protection; • that the eastern wall of the masonry foundation may be reinforced to stabilize the structure • that any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; • that the Commission's approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding amended findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 24th day of August 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (MG-motion, NM-2nd, all-yes).

The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application to repoint the masonry, construct a new entryway, build a fence, and other site improvements as adopted by the HLPC. (JM-motion, KM-2nd, all-yes).

items.title: #48 (44) North Front Street: Painting & signage
items.discussion:
The applicants, Ashley Molesso and Chess Needham, presented the plan to install signage and
paint the storefront of their soon to open business.  “The Everywhere Shop”, a Queer and Trans-owned
stationery and gift company based in Kingston, New York called Ash + Chess has been in business for over 5
years, wholesaling greeting cards, art prints, stickers, clothing, and books to retailers and direct to customers
throughout the United States, Canada, Europe, and Asia. A. Molesso explained that they prepared for the
commissions three different color schemes and secured a fourth historic color palette to incorporate into a final
option that was not originally provided. Commissioners, Staff, and applicant discussed the project at length.
The consensus was that the applicant’s signage would not be as critical as the building mass and the trim.  The
new code does provide for encouraging the use of historic colors.  After a good deal of debate and working the
color panels back and forth, the Commissions were able to settle on a common ground on the original proposal
which incorporated two historic colors manufactured by Sherwin Williams.

The Commissions reviewed the wall signage for the business on the upper level of the building front and the
signage proposed beneath the Pike Plan Canopy.  Staff noted that the one sign cannot have two separate Boards
under the code (which has not changed from what was previously the regulations).  The Commissions noted
that provided the signage complies within the parameters of the regulations, they are agreeable.  Insurance will
also be required.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed installation of 3 signs and painting of 48 (44) N. Front Street in the Stockade Historic District by Ashley Molesso, if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-26, of the City of Kingston's Form-Based Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: • that the proposed work is to take place at the two story store front building on the south side of North Front Street located between Wall and Crown Streets and which the July 1987 Building Structure Inventory form prepared by the Friends of Historic Kingston states that it could date to as early as the 1840s but that an exact date of construction would be hard to determine, and that the shop once housed H. Houghtaling (1894), news dealer James McIntrye (1901)" - subsequent businesses included painters, barbers, beverages, a tavern, Artistic Beauty Salon, and Arties Bar & Grill; • that the applicant shall paint the structure the following colors: Main Building Structure - Sherwin Williams Historic Color "Orchid" #SW0071, Accent/Trim - Sherwin Williams Historic Color "Audrey's Blush" #SW9001, Logo "Everywhere" - Valspar "Autumn Enchantment" #2001-1A, and the word "Shop" - Valspar "The Crowd Roars" #8001-38E; • that the applicant may install three signs - one painted on the second-floor facade that reads "Everywhere Shop", a second shall hang from the Pike Plan and face the sidewalk and read "Everywhere Shop: You Belong Here! ", and the third sign shall hand from the Pike Plan and read " Everywhere Shop", provided all signs comply with standards under the newly adopted FBC sign regulations; • that the owner shall provide the City of Kingston with insurance naming them as additionally insured as required under Section 358-9; • that any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; • that the Commission's approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding amended findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 24th day of August 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (MG-motion, KM-2nd, all-yes).

The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application to repaint the structure’s Wall Street face in the following colors: Main Building Structure - Sherwin Williams Historic Color "Orchid" #SW0071, Accent/Trim - Sherwin Williams Historic Color "Audrey's Blush" #SW9001, Logo "Everywhere" - Valspar "Autumn Enchantment" #2001-1A, and the word "Shop" - Valspar "The Crowd Roars" #8001-38E; and to concur with the approval of the 3 signs for the business. (NM-motion, KM-2nd, all-yes).

items.title: #6 Adams Street: Construction of new rear deck with staircase and refurbish existing stairs for childcare use
items.owner: Catholic Charities of the Archdiocese of New York
items.discussion:
NOTE:  Andrea Puetz, Architect for HLPC, recused herself as she is employed by SDA, the
project Architects.

A. Puetz presented the plan, explaining that the goal on the project is to increase usable outdoor space via the
construction of a 16' by 54' deck comprised of galvanized steel painted black and a trex decking material.
Concrete steps leading to a lunch break area for teachers will be restored in-kind.
The new framework of the deck will allow for a “living wall” to be established and a new shade area to be
provided at ground level.  The existing gazebo structure is slated to be removed from the lawn area to have a
larger open usable play area.

There was discussion about painting over the Todd Sumara mural beneath the deck.  Commissioner Grunblatt
advised A. Puetz, to explore the legalities of such work within the context of the 5Pointz Case.  Staff will also
investigate the matter with the City’s Arts and Cultural Director to see what, if any, restrictions may apply.  A.
Puetz will ask if there was any agreement with the artist, but that the work has not been maintained over the
years.

A. Puetz noted that the plans are showing a style of railing in a horizontal configuration.  Given that the use is
for an area to be occupied by small children, she will be looking at modifying the plan to show a vertical
alignment so that it does not become a climbing feature and potential danger.  The Commissioners all agreed
that the change should be made to the design.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed installation of a rear deck at 6 Adams Street in the Rondout Historic District by The New York State Federation of Growers' and Processors’ Associations, Inc. [d/b/a Agri-Business Child Development (ABCD)], if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-26, of the City of Kingston's Form-Based Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: • that the proposed work is to take place at the two-story Classical Revival St. Peters School building located at the southeastern end of Adams Street and that the January 1977 Building Structure Inventory Form prepared by the Friends of Historic Kingston states "the date 1911 appears on the cornerstone of this building which replaced a church which was previously on this site. The Classical Revival structure is intact and has received no major modern alterations"; • that the applicant will construct a 16' by 54' deck comprised of a galvanized steel support structure with trex decking material, attached to the existing concrete retaining wall at the rear of 6 Adams Street; • that a galvanized steel and trex staircase shall be constructed for movement from the deck down to the playground below that abuts Broadway; • that the applicant shall work with staff to modify the steel railing to provide for a vertical arrangement rather than horizontal; • Any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; • The Commission's approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding amended findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 24th day of August 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (AP-recuse; MG-motion, RT-2nd, all others -yes).

The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to approve the application to construct a 16' by 54' deck on the rear of 6 Adams Street to increase playground space for the occupying school (JM-motion, KM-2nd, all-yes). NOTE FOR RECORD – This was the last formal meeting of the Heritage Area Commission, unless a matter of Coastal Consistency is needed. That function is presently being considered to change over to the Planning Board. Functions of the Heritage Area Commission will be transferred to the HLPC or to staff as desk reviews going forward under the newly adopted Form-based Code. The Heritage Area boundary is still recognized within the city limits and will be accordingly referenced. Staff and other members thanked those who will no longer be at the table for their enthusiasm and participation in making the process a better functioning system. Members were encouraged to submit applications and resumes as other Boards and Commissions are looking for volunteers. Next HLPC Meeting: September 7th, 2023. This meeting was live streamed and available on the City of Kingston YouTube channel: https://www.youtube.com/c/CityofKingstonNY

items.title: Adoption of the HLPC Adoption of the Minutes of August 24th, 2023, Meeting: a. HLPC Decision: No discussion. The Commission voted unanimously to adopt the minutes from the August 24th, 2023, Meeting: (RT-motion, AP-2nd, all yes). HLPC REGULAR BUSINESS:
#93 Fair Street: Replacing Greek Revival front entrance, adding new design elements, and landscape features
items.discussion:
NOTE:  The applicant, R. Arket, was not present when the item was called so the HLPC set the
matter aside until the end of the meeting to see if they appeared. This item was addressed last with the
applicant absent. It was recognized that E. Dickerman had prepared a report assessing the doorway, using
photos which staff had taken and some which had been provided by the applicant. The report had been
circulated to both the Commission members and the applicant in advance of the meeting and copies were also

available at the meeting. M. Grunblatt noted that he had visited the site and asked other Commissioners
present if they had also had the opportunity to view the location. Both N. Morano and R. Tonner stated they
had visited and have firsthand knowledge of the site. Staff recognized that the rendered replica depicts
alterations to the number of side lights and changes to the column and door’s details. Thus, it is not a true
replica. Staff also noted that the doorway is one of the last features of the structure which exists on the
exterior.  M. Grunblatt noted that the structure was severely degraded and that the overall project is
commendable. However, any additions/alteration should remain simple and within the traits of the Greek
Revival design. Rendering a final determination on the project was deemed not possible because the
Commissioners were unable to ask and receive answers to their questions.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to table the item for additional information, noting that staff would relate the discussion to the owner and the request for the applicant to attend the October 5th, 2023, meeting. (RT-motion, KM-2nd, NM, AP, RT -yes).

items.title: #85 Wurts Street: Repainting entire facade
items.discussion:
The applicant/owner, Kristin Jaeger, presented plans to repaint 85 Wurts Street, the former
Presbyterian Parsonage, in a quasi-monotone color scheme – taking inspiration from historical records which
indicated to her that ‘larger houses situated in brighter locations could be acceptably painted in darker colors,
as opposed to smaller dwellings in darker settings.’ After the original submission, staff reached out to discuss
possible options on the color scheme.   K. Jaeger stated that they have amended the paint options to include
historic colors sourced from Historic New England, Benjamin Moore, and California Colors. She presented
various color schemes photoshopped on the structure to demonstrate how using different shades/color choices
might be less of an enhancement to the architectural details, because of shadowing effects which would result,
or that contrasts would not do justice to certain elements of the building.  Her final proposal was to paint the
body and trim in Brattle Spruce by California Paints, the windows in Black HC-190 by Benjamin Moore, and
the front entrance door in Danish Pine by California Paints. Commission members agreed that this
combination/ color scheme was appropriate and enhanced the structure’s features better than adding
additional accent colors.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed repainting at 85 Wurts Street in the Rondout Historic District, by owner Kristin Jaeger, if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-26, of the City of Kingston's Form Based Zoning Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: • that the proposed work is to take place at the two-story brick Italianate structure located on the southwestern corner of the intersection of Wurts Street and West Pierpont Street which was constructed circa 1863 to serve as the parsonage for the neighboring Rondout Presbyterian Church; • that the applicant shall paint the main body of the structure and its trim in Brattle Spruce by California Paints LRV 5.9; • that the existing wooden windows shall be scraped to remove loose paint, with restoration as needed, and repainted in Black HC-190 by Benjamin Moore: • that the front door shall be painted Danish Pine by California Paints 32.96; • that the stone windowsills and the date of construction stone shall not be painted; • any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; • the Commission's approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 21st day of September 2023, the Commission voted to grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (MG – motion, RT-2nd, NM, AP – yes, KM – absent).

items.title: #70 North Front Street: O+ Mural
items.discussion:
Dr. J. Cohen and B. Cohen, owners; and Lindsey Wolkowicz of the O+ Festival, were present
before the commission. L. Wolkowicz presented the mural project on behalf of the Cohens. L. Wolkowicz
clarified that the proposed mural is by a well-known and experienced artist and the subject covers an actor,
writer, and living activist who resides in Stone Ridge. It was noted that the location was a second choice for
this installation but is recognized as one which has high visibility.  The goal of the mural is to support the
LGBTQIA+ community and to educate viewers, along with a QR code, about the mural’s subject.
The HLPC asked about vandalism in the past and L. Wolkowicz noted that there has been graffiti done to
some of the murals and that they have been able to address it quickly.  Asked if the mural itself tends to attract
some of this negative activity, and the response was it was not clear if that is the case, but she felt that some of
it felt targeted to the O+ efforts and mission.  She noted that with time, the materials that are used are
improved and better quality so that the actual murals are holding up better to the weather elements.
L. Wolkowicz also clarified the following:
• O+ chooses a type of paint that will not adversely affect the structure.
• That the mural proposed at 70 N Front shall incorporate existing yellows and greens sourced from the
structure’s North Front Street face and the submitted digitized rendering is not accurate to reflect
those colors.
• O+ is responsible for the mural’s care for the life of the mural. If vandalism occurs, O+ will respond
within 24 hours, or as quickly as possible.
• O+ asks that the mural be up for at least 3 years because of the time and value it takes to install.
However, the owner can choose to keep it for longer if desired.
• O+ is the broker between the property owner and the artist. Any agreement is valid only for the current
owner. If the property sells, the future owner can choose to remove the mural if they please, before the
3-year period.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed painting of a mural for the O+ Festival by David Puck at 70 N. Front Street which is owned by Dr. Joseph Cohen OD , if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-26, of the City of Kingston’s Form Based Zoning Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district for the following reasons: • that the proposed work is to take place at the circa 1880s two-story framed commercial building located at the southwestern corner of the intersection of North Front Street and Crown Street, and which functioned as a saloon in the 1890s, as a shoemaker’s shop in 1915, as a tailor’s shop from 1921 until 1940, Frank’s Sport Shop in 1950 until 1974, and as Copyland in the 1980s; • that the mural shall be located on the westward-facing clapboard-sided wall of 70 N Front Street which is adjacent to a municipal parking lot; - that the mural will be done using a water-based primer and topcoat, acrylic paint that will not adversely impact the clapboard siding; • that the artwork shall be produced by David Puck, a queer muralist and performer based in Brooklyn, NY, and will honor Celeste Lecesne who is the founder of The Trevor Project and The Future Perfect Project and shall conform with the samples provided to the HLPC via the artist’s portfolio; • that a final mock-up of the proposed mural shall be submitted to the City Planning Office for the file; • that maintenance of the mural shall be addressed within a reasonable notice and will be the responsibility of O+ Organization if there is chipping, graffiti or other deterioration to the installation; • that it is understood that the mural will remain in place for a period of 3 years; - that the artist and/or owner will submit application to the DPW for permitting when installation takes place to cover use of the public parking area; • any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; • the Commission’s approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston’s Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 21st day of September 2023, the Commission voted to grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (MG-motion, NM-2nd, all others-yes).

items.title: #169 Abeel Street: Replacement of door along Ravine Street
#54 Gill Street: Voluntary presentation of exterior rehabilitation, cupola modifications, window restoration, porch repair & modifications
items.discussion:
Staff stated that the applicants had reached out with respect to improvements which they are
proposing for their home at 54 Gill Street. This property was recently determined individually eligible for
listing on the State & National Registers of Historic Places by the AHRS, the consultants for the 2020-2023
CLG grant. As such, the applicants, Amiee Gardner & David Linnard, voluntarily (and without cost) opted to
have the project presented to the HLPC for feedback on the work they propose to rehabilitate the property. A.
Gardner & D. Linnard presented to the Commissioners the significant work they’ve already done to stabilize
and rehabilitate the structure since purchasing it from the city circa 2017. The applicant/owners discussed the
following:
• Replacing the existing, non-original, ground floor door with an existing and possibly historic wooden
door sourced from their shed/garage. This door will also be aligned with the position of the original
arches front entrance located on the porch. This door will become the structure’s primary entrance.
• Restoring the front porch in-kind such that as many of the original features are retrained. Douglas fir
was mentioned as the primary wood to be used due to its resiliency.
• Restoring and/or rebuilding the structure’s wooden windows.
• Creation of a penthouse in the cupola with a small deck and railing atop the roof. The Commission
discussed the proposed design of the railing on this upper element, noting that it might not be the best
choice for the era of the structure, and recognizing that it might be best to undertake a little more
research on this aspect.
• Although in the original re-submission there was a staircase to the right of the front porch which was to
be newly constructed, that stair has been removed from the plan to keep the building more symmetrical
and original in appearance.
• Listing the property on the State and National Registers and securing federal and/or state tax incentives
to defray the costs of their rehabilitation.
• The couple shall return to the commission and remain in contact with the Planning Department as they
proceed with work.

Commission members present were grateful to have the information shared.  They noted that staff could share
information with the owners on incentive programs at various government levels.  The HLPC was encouraged
that the owners are taking such care with the restoration and recognized that it is a difficult task.  K. McEvoy
stated that as a nearby resident he had information which could be shared with the owners to assist with their
work.
NO ACTION was taken.

items.title: Adoption of the HLPC Adoption of the Minutes of September 21st, 2023, Meeting:
#93 Fair Street: Replacing Greek Revival front entrance, adding new design elements, and landscape features
items.discussion:
Ryan Arket was present at the meeting. Chairman Grunblatt recognized that the item had been
tabled at last month’s meeting, requesting that the owner be present.  R’ Arket was asked to review the plans
for the entryway, with staff identifying the opening had recently been covered over. R. Arket stated that he had

looked at the door with his carpenter and that he intends to replicate the door and frame out of mahogany. He
said that the entry had deteriorated and that he wanted a new door but that he was open to replicating it to
look like the original.  The Commission reviewed the frame and window configuration on the sidelights noting
that the drawing for the replication submitted did not match the number of windows as in the original.  It was
also noted that the existing door had a window and multiple lower panels, and the drawing of the “replica” was
a solid door with different panel arrangements and therefore not a replica but a concept.  He said that his
carpenter thought that it would look better but that he was willing to do what the Commission thought was
best.  M. Grunblatt asked about the condition of the original door and whether the door could be restored.  S.
Cahill stated that she wanted to see effort made to reusing the door and that the condition looked as though
restoration could be achieved.  R. Arket said that he preferred a door without glass and that he wanted to
create a solid door for the replacement.  He said that as the property owner he had the choice to replace it if he
wanted.  S. Cahill said that the Commission has the authority to review and decide on these matters.
Commissioners discussed that if the door itself could be restored, then possibly the frame surround could be
accordingly replicated and that would be a fair compromise.  M. Grunblatt asked if the owner could look into
restoration. R. Arket said that it was not possible because the door was gone.  S. Cahill asked the applicant
why he deceived staff and sent an email saying that the door was covered to protect it from the elements. R.
Arket said that he never lied, he just did not say the door was missing, that he was waiting for the Commission
to meet.

NOTE: S. Cahill excused herself from the meeting to reach out to the City Corp. Counsel. The Commission
asked the property owner to wait to be recalled and took up the next item while S. Cahill reached M.
Jankowski by phone.  Upon returning to the meeting, S. Cahill advised the Commission to enter executive
session to discuss the matter with the Assistant Corporation Counsel.  (AP – motion, KM- 2nd – MG, NM-yes
to enter the session).  After reopening meeting (MG – motion, KM – 2nd – NM, AP -yes) , the Commission
recalled R. Arket to the table to finish the discussion.

M. Grunblatt asked R. Arket where the door was and if he still had it on the site.  R. Arket said that the door
had been disposed of by his contractors.  He said that there was a miscommunication with his Spanish
speaking contractors.  He told the Commission that the original plan was to replace the door with a replica.
His contractors knew the original plan and had moved forward with the removal when he wasn’t there after he
had told them to leave it in place.  M. Grunblatt offered to assist in asking the contractors where they brought
the door so that it could be tracked down. M. Grunblatt asked the applicant to continue to try to locate the
door and asked the Commission to move forward with additional requests by the applicant.

R. Arket requested the ability to construct a new entry stoop to replace the one that is existing. He explained
that the existing construction is concrete with a faux stone tiles adhered to the façade.  He would like to
replace it with a concrete base with a bluestone façade and stairs.  S. Cahill noted that a new stair and steps
will need to be constructed to code and that there may be adjustment in riser and tread dimensions than are
currently in place.  The owner will need to submit exact drawings to the Building Department to obtain a
permit and at that time they will review for compliance.  Along with the new steps, a metal railing will be
installed that would be period specific and give the appearance of a black wrought iron.  AN example was
provided by the owner.

Next, R. Arket explained that he would like to add a bluestone garden wall that would be about 1ft. high and
would be located along the Fair Street sidewalk and along the one side yard and partially through the side yard
closest to the corner.  The wall would not run all the way to the corner but would enclose an area along either
side of the staircase for landscaping.  The Commission agreed to both plans for the wall and the stairs.

R. Arket stated that he is proposing to add columns at the corners of the structure and corbels at the roof line
overhang.  The Commission disagreed with the addition of those features, noting that they are not considered
to be accurate in depicting the structures architectural past.  Both elements would provide a “false” façade to
the structure and thus have a negative impact to the district.  A. Puetz noted that keeping a simpler face on the
building was more representative of structure.

Lastly, the owner presented the Board with a style light fixture and explained that he would like to have one
installed at the front entry on Fair Street and one at the door entry on Franklin Street.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed replacement of the Greek Revival entrance at 93 Fair Street, in the Fair Street Historic District, by applicant Ryan Arket, if done according to the plans reviewed at this meeting and according to the procedures stipulated in Section 405-26, of the City of Kingston's Form Based Zoning Code, is compatible with the historic character of the district, noting the following reasons, conditions and limitations: • that the proposed work is to take place at the 2 and 1/2 story framed Greek Revival single family dwelling built circa 1860 and which is located at the northwestern corner of the intersection of Fair Street and Franklin Street; • that a decision on the entryway is TABLED for information on the doorway disposal and contractor submitted to staff for HLPC; • that the applicant MAY NOT add simple corbels, as they are not original to the structure; • that the applicant IS NOT PERMITTED to install fixed columns at building corners as presented, as they are not original to the structure; • that the applicant be permitted to install a light fixture, as submitted, near the front entryway and at the side entry door that conforms with city code; • that the applicant shall be permitted to improve the front steps with bluestone as described and change the railing to one that conforms with the Greek Revival style and conforms to building code; • that the applicant shall construct a garden wall along the front and side yards to beautify the landscape using bluestone material, and at a 1' height maximum; • any changes or additions to the plans and/or work specifically described and outlined in the submitted application will be subject to further review by our commission prior to the work being carried out; • the Commission's approval does not obviate the need for a Building Permit from the City of Kingston's Building Safety Division or any other required approvals from relevant coordinating agencies; Based on the preceding findings of fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 5th day of October 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the work as described herein and in its application to the Commission, such notice to be subject to the conditions contained in the foregoing motion. (MG-motion, NM-2nd, KM, AP, -yes).

items.title: #8-14 N Front Street: Installation of four vinyl banners on Fair Street side requiring minor waiver review

items.title: Adoption of the HLPC Adoption of the Minutes of October 5th, 2023, Meeting:
#93 Fair Street: Replacing Greek Revival front entrance, adding new design elements, and landscape features
items.discussion:
The owner, Ryan Arket, and his contractor/carpenter, Keith Baker, presented plans to
construct a replacement entrance and front door. K. Baker stated his qualifications and past work
experience and stated that the entrance and door were in severe disrepair. Based on his observations, he felt
the entrance and door were not salvageable. He admitted to not taking measurements, photos or recording
detail of the deterioration and conditions prior to the feature’s removal.

Staff and the Commission stated their request that the Secretary of Interior’s Standards for Reconstruction
be followed during the production of the new feature. The number of side lights, transom lights,
dimensions, trim detail (or lack thereof) should match identically. Commissioners were amenable to the
door being produced to as a 2/2 solid panel door. The commission was requested to authorize staff to
finalize the entrance and door details with the owner, and with the assistance of the Commission’s
architect, Andrea Puetz.

R. Arket and K. Baker questioned the Commission and staff about adding decorative corner features that
resembled fixed columns, eve-mounted corbels, trim over the 1st floor window lintels, and a plain skirt at
the wooden façade’s base. The Commission maintained that adding features to embellish the structure’s
Greek-revival appearance is not permissible under the Secretary of Interior’s Standards and does not align
with the character of the historic district. Therefore, the corbels and corner columns were not entertained.
Adding simple trim over the 1st floor windows and a plain siding skirt was accepted. The Commission also
agreed to allow for corner trim, only in a straight linear fashion be allowed, without any decorative trim or
top.

S. Cahill did inform the commissioners that the columns were already created and R. Arket admitted to
“jumping the gun” in their production. S. Cahill read for the commission, applicants, and staff the hardship
clause in the code – which the applicant did not qualify for, as the production of the columns falls under the
category of “self-inflicted” hardship. If the applicant may still choose to appeal the HLPC’s decision to
Zoning Board of Appeals.

The Commission reviewed the replacement of the garage doors on the detached structure fronting Franklin
Street.  The specification for doors from Richards-Wilcox Classic (L-138) from their Landmark Series in black,
and with divided windows, and recessed smooth plank paneling was shared, and the Commission accepted.  It was
noted that they closely resembled the current degraded doors.

The last item reviewed was the side door entryway.  R. Arket stated that they had previously had a metal
awing which has been removed.  He requested approval to install a simple covered portico structure to
provide minimal coverage at the doorway.

The Commission noted that new elevation plans will need to be submitted identifying the features as
discussed during the meeting.  These will need review by staff and Commissioner Puetz, prior to any work
being started.

items.discussion:

items.title: #52 St. James St: Review of & recommendation for State & National Register Nomination
items.discussion:
Staff informed the commissioners that Marissa Marvelli was hired by the property owner,
Miriam Lipson, to research and nominate 52 St. James Street to the State & National Registers of Historic
Places which will directly assist the site’s rehabilitation through the state and federal tax programs. All the
commission must do is vote to support the property for listing.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed New York State & National Register of Historic Places Nomination for 52 St. James Street, is consistent with the goals and mission of the Historic Programs in the City of Kingston and will provide for continued protection and preservation of this resource. The Commission finds the following:  that the proposed nomination is for the William H. and Mary M. Romeyn House is a one-and-one-half- story, wood-frame house with eclectic picturesque details that mostly reflect the Gothic Revival style. It was originally built ca. 1853 as a front-gabled rectangular volume with two principal rooms and a side hall. It was expanded with two symmetrical gabled side wings ca. 1870.  that the structure is significant under Criterion C in the area of architecture as an intact example of a mid-nineteenth-century Gothic Revival cottage that reflects strong associations with the Picturesque Movement, which swept much of the nation in the decades before and after the Civil War and represented a departure from the predominant Neoclassical style. Originally built ca. 1853 as a single front-gable volume by Edward Brink, a local architect and carpenter responsible for noteworthy buildings in the area including the First Reformed Dutch Church of Kingston, the house was expanded ca..1870 with symmetrical side wings. The expansion was undertaken by the Romeyns, a socially prominent Kingston couple who lived in the house from 1858 to 1880. As the editor and publisher of several Kingston newspapers, William Romeyn was an influential voice in Whig and later Republican politics. The alterations made for the Romeyns included not only the expansion of the original two- room and side-hall floor plan, but also the addition of architectural embellishments including an elaborately carved Gothic-style gable screen framed by chamfered trusses. No other known surviving example in Kingston has the same level of intricacy. Based on the preceding Findings of Fact, it is proposed to resolve that on the 2nd day of November 2023, the Commission grant a Preservation Notice of Action to the above referenced Applicant, for the Nomination to the State and National Registers of Historic Places as described herein to the Commission. (RT-motion, NM-2nd, KM, AP, MG-yes).

items.title: St. Joseph’s Parish Complex Historic District Nomination. Review and recommendation for State and National Register Nomination. SBLs: 48.331-6-13 & 14, 56.91-3-1, 56.91-2-23.110
items.owner: St Joseph’s Church & Kingston Ops Zone II LLC

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to find as fact that the proposed New York State & National Register of Historic Places Nomination for 52 St. James Street, is consistent with the goals and mission of the Historic Programs in the City of Kingston and will provide for continued protection and preservation of this resource. The Commission finds the following: • The 51. Joseph's Parish Complex is significant under criterion C in the area of Architecture as an excellent example of the evolution and growth of an ecclesiastical campus in the heart of the uptown neighborhood in Kingston, New York. Erected in several campaigns over more than a century, the buildings of St, Joseph's parish represent a variety of architectural styles and building types, designed by locally (and sometime nationally) prominent architects. The parish complex expanded over time both to meet the needs of a growing congregation and because opportunities arose to acquire land adjacent to their existing facilities. The congregation clearly prioritized proximity of its services and it was able to create a geographically and visually contiguous campus in the middle of Kingston. The small complex also exemplifies a typical Roman Catholic Church parish type, including a fu1l complement of buildings, such as a church, rectory, convent and two schools, built in close proximity to promote a stable social and moral foundation and a strong program of religious education for immigrants in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. • The complex comprises six contributing buildings were all designed-or substantially redesigned-for St. Joseph's parish. The church building at the southeast corner of Main and Wall Streets was originally erected in 1832-33 by the Dutch Reformed Church of Kingston with a Greek Revival design by architect Henry Rector. A few decades later, St. Joseph's Catholic Church purchased the property and updated the building to its current appearance during two separate campaigns: the first, carried out in 1868-69 introduced Romanesque elements designed by J. A. Wood; the second, in 1898, added the Gothic Revival facade designed by William J. Beardsley. The adjacent Second empire-style rectory at 242 Wall Street was constructed by the parish in 1874. The Italian Renaissance Revival-style school at 236 Wall Street and the Mediterranean Revival-style convent at 59 Pearl Streel were both completed in 1913 to the designs of Arthur C. Longyear. The mid-century school at 231Wall Street was built 1963 to the designs of Albert E. Milliken. A utilitarian three-car garage and maids’ quarters was constructed 1939 behind the rectory. • The complex retains significant architectural integrity from its period of significance and reflects the evolution of not only architectural style, but also the growth of the St. Joseph’s parish and the Kingston Catholic community over the better part of a century, beginning with the construction of the original church in 1832 and extending through completion of the 2nd school building in 1963. The Commission voted in favor of rendering the action a Type II under SEQR and to endorse the proposed district nomination as presented. The mayor would be notified of this determination so that a recommendation letter can be submitted to the NYSHPO. (MG-motion, KM-2nd; NM, RT- yes; AP - recused)

items.title: § 360- 35-39 Article VI: Exemptions for Historic Properties. Review and recommendation to Common Council for the readoption of local tax law with proposed amendments
items.discussion:
S. Cahill presented to the commission the Planning & Assessor Departments intention to seek
authorization from the Common Council to reactivate ARTICLE VI: § 360-35-39 - Exemptions for Historic
Properties, of the municipal tax code, which was initially adopted by the Common Council in 1998 and readopted in
2004 before expiring in 2009.

Staff view this local real property tax exemption as a crucial tool to financially incentivize preservation community
wide. Eligible properties include any locally designated property, SR & NR properties, and structures within historic
districts. The local historic preservation program would be a tax exemption on real property value for the city of
Kingston portion of taxes, whereas the state and federal programs are income tax credit programs. Commissioners
voiced overwhelming support for the program.

M. Grunblatt noted that in the past the commission did not have staff to support and educate applicants about the
program, which was why it was not taken advantage of by more residents. K. McEvoy also noted that this program
will be a huge asset to the residents of the proposed Wilbur Historic District and the Ponckhockie Historic District.
S. Cahill informed the Commission that readoption of this program will be scheduled at the same time as the
Common Council’s review of the proposed Wilbur and Ponckhockie Historic Districts and Temple Emanuel
Landmarking.

decisions.text: The Commission voted unanimously to render the action a Type II under SEQR and to endorse the proposed readoption of the tax exemption as presented. (MG-motion, NM-2nd; RT, KM, AP- yes)
